enumTypeRef.$comment: c25: the REF-ONLY enum specifier, kept for the param/cast positions (declHeadForParam, castTypeBase). The declaration-head positions route through the UNIFIED `enumSpec` (below). Mirrors structTypeRef.

enumTypeSpecifier.$comment: C23 6.7.2.2 (D-CSUBSET-ENUM-UNDERLYING-TYPE, FC17): the OPTIONAL `: <integer-type>` clause that fixes an enum's underlying type — `enum E : unsigned char { A }`. A SEQUENCE `[Colon, castTypeBase]` (castTypeBase is the qualifier-free/pointer-free base type-name — `unsigned char`, `int`, a typedef, NOT `int *`). It carries `commitRequiresTypeName` with `requireKnownType` polarity (MIRRORS `alignasTypeName`): the enum-underlying `:` collides with the pre-existing anonymous enum-typed struct bit-field `enum Color : 4;`, so the parser SPECULATIVELY tries this clause after the `:` and the binder triage commits ONLY on a real type (keyword/tag-led base → Rule 1; a KNOWN typedef → Rule 2); a bit-field WIDTH (an int-constant `4`, or a value/unknown identifier `enum Tag : SOME_WIDTH`) ROLLS BACK, leaving the `:` for the member-level bit-field grammar. SEMANTICS live in the semantic tier (DeclarationRule.enumUnderlyingType): the resolved integer TypeKind becomes the enum's underlying scalar (scalars[0]) and each enumerator's value is range-checked against it (fail-loud S_InvalidEnumUnderlyingType on a non-integer, S_EnumeratorValueOutOfRange on overflow).
enumTypeSpecifier.$tfc101Comment: TF-C101: this clause's base is `enumUnderlyingBase`, NOT the type-name base `castTypeBase` it used to share. THE TWO POSITIONS STOPPED BEING THE SAME GRAMMAR when `castTypeBase` was widened to admit composite DEFINITIONS (see that rule) — read `enumUnderlyingBase` for why sharing became actively wrong here, and why splitting is a real distinction rather than a copy.

enumUnderlyingBase.$comment:
TF-C101: the base type-specifier of the C23 enum-underlying clause (`enum E : unsigned char { A }`). Vocabulary-IDENTICAL to what `castTypeBase` was before this cycle, and deliberately so: the ONE thing it must not do is admit a composite specifier WITH A BODY.
★ WHY IT EXISTS RATHER THAN REUSING `castTypeBase`. This slot is IMMEDIATELY followed by the enumerator-list `{`. Once `castTypeBase` routes `struct` through the unified `structSpec` — whose `{optional structBody}` is greedy — `enum E : struct Foo { A }` binds `{ A }` to the STRUCT, leaving the enum with no enumerator list. MEASURED: `clang -std=c23` binds it the same way (`redefinition of 'Foo'`, `unknown type name 'A'`), so the greedy reading is not wrong about C — C23 6.7.2.2 really does spell the clause `: specifier-qualifier-list`, and a specifier-qualifier-list really may carry a member list. But MEASURED in DSS, that reading is strictly WORSE HERE: the struct body then desyncs on `A`, the whole speculative clause rolls back, and one precise `S_InvalidEnumUnderlyingType` becomes a NINE-diagnostic parse cascade (`S_UnknownType` on the enum, `P_NoAlternativeMatched` on the `:`, six more downstream). A ref-only base keeps the `{` for the enum, so the analyzer receives an intact enum whose underlying type is a struct and rejects it by CONSTRAINT — one diagnostic, at the right tier, naming the right thing. That is better than clang here, and it is the behavior this repo already pinned.
★ THIS IS A DISTINCTION, NOT DUPLICATION — and the distinction is the reason the shared rule had to end. A type-NAME position (`sizeof`, cast, `_Generic`, compound literal) is closed by `)`, so a definition there is unambiguous and useful; this position is closed by the very `{` a definition would eat, so a definition here can only ever be a constraint violation whose diagnostic we would be degrading to buy nothing. Widening BOTH from one rule would have traded a real diagnostic for a construct no one can write correctly.
★ THE DRIFT RISK, STATED SO IT STAYS LOUD: a NEW base type form added to `castTypeBase` will not appear here automatically. That is survivable exactly because the failure mode is a parse ERROR in the enum-underlying slot, never a silent mis-read — but a form that belongs in both (a new integer specifier) must be added to both in the SAME commit.

enumSpec.$comment: c25 D-CSUBSET-UNIFIED-COMPOSITE-SPECIFIER: the UNIFIED enum specifier — `enum {opt tag} {opt underlying-type} {opt body}`. Mirrors `structSpec`: ONE rule for define (`enum E { A, B }`) and reference (`enum E`), the SOLE EnumKeyword candidate in the 4 body-bearing alts → non-speculative direct descent. Dual-mode binder via `definesWhenChild: enumBody`. The enumerator-list (with trailing comma) lives in `enumBody`. FC17 (D-CSUBSET-ENUM-UNDERLYING-TYPE / D-PARSE-SPECULATIVE-OPTIONAL): the optional C23 `: <integer-type>` clause (`enumTypeSpecifier`) sits between the tag and the body as a SPECULATIVE optional so `enum E : unsigned char { A }` fixes the underlying type while the pre-existing anonymous enum-typed bit-field `enum Color : 4;` still parses (the clause is TRIED after the `:` and ROLLS BACK to the bit-field reading when a type doesn't follow — the whole point of the speculative-optional engine capability).

enumBody.$comment: c25: the brace-delimited enumerator list, factored out of `enumSpec` as the define-vs-reference discriminator. NOT a scope rule (enumerators bind into the enclosing enumSpec's scope, then lift to the enclosing namespace scope per fieldChildren.liftToEnclosingScope). Enumerator-list shape (optional list, trailing comma) identical to the former `enumSpecifierBody` tail.

topLevelDecl.$comment: C declaration = decl-specifiers init-declarator-list? `;` (or a function-definition block tail). The init-declarator-list is OPTIONAL: a bare `struct P { … };` / `enum E { … };` is a type-only declaration (head introduces the tag, no object declared) — the semantic tier mints the type from the head and emits a TypeDecl; a head that introduces NO tag with no declarator (`int ;`) is a C6.7p2 'declares nothing' constraint violation (fail-loud). A trailing declarator (`struct P { … } v;`) or a block tail (`struct Tri mkTri(void){…}`) takes the normal global/function path.
topLevelDecl.$tfc77Comment: TF-C77 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-LEADING-WITH-STORAGE-CLASS, mode 2): `declAttrRun` — the MID-POSITION attribute slot between the type head and the declarator list (`static int SQLITE_NOINLINE f(…)`, `int __attribute__((weak)) gv;`). It is a SIBLING of `topLevelHead`, never a child (see declAttrRun's own comment for the type-hijack reasoning). Because it is a named rule over a lone `{repeat}` it is ALWAYS emitted, so the row's post-strip role children are FIXED: [topLevelHead(0), declAttrRun(1), initDeclaratorList(2), topLevelDeclTail(3)] with a declarator list, [topLevelHead(0), declAttrRun(1), topLevelDeclTail(2)] without one. The row's `declaratorList` moved 1 → 2 and `kindByChild.childPath` [2,0] → [3,0] IN THE SAME COMMIT (the `structSpec` `name: 1 → 2` precedent) — leaving either at its old value MIS-LOWERS every function definition in the TU.

topLevelHead.$comment: Top-level head: a keyword type specifier (`typeSpecifierSeq`, e.g. `int`/`unsigned long`), a struct/union/enum composite specifier (`topLevelCompositeSpec` — the SPECULATIVE body-vs-ref alt), OR a lone Identifier (typedef name). The OUTER alt is NON-speculative: FIRST(typeSpecifierSeq)={type keywords}, FIRST(topLevelCompositeSpec)={struct,union,enum}, FIRST(Identifier)={ident} are pairwise disjoint — so a plain `int x;` routes DIRECTLY to typeSpecifierSeq (NO extra wrapper node, preserving the pre-existing tree shape) and only a struct/union/enum lead enters the single-level speculation that closes D-CSUBSET-STRUCT-BODY-VARDECL-POSITION. topLevel stays non-speculative: `struct` routes unambiguously to topLevelDecl.

topLevelCompositeSpec.$comment: c25 D-CSUBSET-UNIFIED-COMPOSITE-SPECIFIER: the struct/union/enum SPECIFIER at a top-level declaration head — now ONE unified rule per keyword (`structSpec`/`unionSpec`/`enumSpec`), each covering BOTH the body form (`struct P { … }`) AND the bare tag reference (`struct P`) via an internal `{optional body}`. The three candidates have pairwise-DISJOINT 1-token FIRSTs (StructKeyword/UnionKeyword/EnumKeyword), so the predictive prune leaves EXACTLY ONE survivor for any composite lead → the parser's unique-production DIRECT DESCENT (parser.cpp ~1804-1844) dispatches it NON-speculatively. The member body therefore parses with NO speculation budget — the c25 fix for `struct sqlite3`'s large body (the former body-vs-ref probe budget-capped at 4096 tokens). `speculative`/`lookahead` are retained but moot under the unique-survivor direct descent (kept so a future non-disjoint addition still has a probe budget). The enum body's trailing-comma enumerator-list parses cleanly (the schema compiler propagates nested-nullable FOLLOW via recomputeAltExpectedSets).

topLevelDeclTail.$comment: FIRST(block)={BlockOpen} vs {EndStatement} — disjoint. A block tail makes the FIRST init-declarator a function DEFINITION (semantic-tier checks enforce: exactly one declarator, named, fn-suffix-bearing, no initializer); an EndStatement tail makes every declarator a global variable.

singleDeclSpecifier.$comment: C11/C23 6.7.5 (D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS): `alignasSpec` (`_Alignas`/`alignas`) joins the top-level declaration-specifier alts. Its FIRST = {AlignasKeyword, AlignasLegacyKeyword} is DISJOINT from StaticKeyword / attrSpec's AttributeKeyword / stdAttr's BracketOpen, so the repeat stays predictively pruned (non-speculative). It is stripped from the positional-child count (specifierPrefix: declSpecifiers on topLevelDecl) and IGNORED by the linkage scan (linkageSpecifierIgnoredRules). FC16 (D-CSUBSET-NORETURN): the bare `_Noreturn` keyword (NoreturnKeyword) likewise joins the alts — FIRST {NoreturnKeyword} disjoint from all the above, so no speculation impact; it is stripped from the child count and IGNORED by the linkage scan (linkageSpecifierIgnoredKinds); the SEMANTIC noreturn scan reads it. The attribute forms (`[[noreturn]]`/`__attribute__((noreturn))`) ride the existing attrSpec/stdAttr alts. FC17 (D-CSUBSET-CONSTEXPR, C23 6.7.1): the `constexpr` storage-class specifier (ConstexprKeyword) joins the alts — FIRST {ConstexprKeyword} disjoint from all the above (a distinct exact-match keyword; `const` is a headQualifier, not a specifier, so no prefix collision), stripped from the child count like the others. At FILE scope it IS a linkage specifier: C23 6.2.2p3 gives a file-scope constexpr object INTERNAL linkage, so topLevelDecl's linkageSpecifiers maps the keyword text to {binding:local} (it is deliberately NOT in that row's linkageSpecifierIgnoredKinds). The SEMANTIC constexpr validation (Pass 2 validateConstexprDeclarator) reads it via semantics.constexpr.keywordToken.
singleDeclSpecifier.$threadLocalComment: TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL, C11/C23 6.7.1): the `_Thread_local`/`thread_local` twin keywords (the _Alignof/alignof spelling precedent) join the alts — FIRST {ThreadLocalKeyword, ThreadLocalC23Keyword} disjoint from every other branch (distinct exact-match keywords), stripped from the child count like the others. The repeat admits both orders with `static` (`static thread_local` / `thread_local static`). NOT a linkage-changing specifier: the topLevelDecl row maps both spellings to {threadStorage:true} — a file-scope thread_local object keeps EXTERNAL linkage (6.2.2 untouched); Pass 1's specifier scan marks the symbol isThreadLocal and Pass 2's validateThreadLocalDeclarator enforces 6.7.1.
singleDeclSpecifier.$tfc79Comment: TF-C79 (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-FUNCTION-SPECIFIER, C99 6.7.4): the `inline` FUNCTION specifier joins the alts — FIRST {InlineKeyword} disjoint from every other branch (a distinct exact-match keyword), so the repeat stays predictively pruned and every ordering (`static inline` / `inline static` / `inline __attribute__((...))`) comes free. ★ ONE TOKEN KIND FOR ALL THREE SPELLINGS: the keyword table maps `inline`, `__inline` and `__inline__` to the SINGLE kind `InlineKeyword`. MEASURED against `/usr/bin/clang -std=c99 -O0 -c` + `nm`: `inline int p(int){…}` and `__inline int p(int){…}` produce the IDENTICAL symbol state (`U _p` — no external definition), so the spellings are synonyms and giving `__inline` its own kind would invite a semantics split that does not exist. The C99-vs-GNU89 divergence rides the LANGUAGE MODE and the `gnu_inline` ATTRIBUTE, never the spelling. ★ It is NOT a linkage specifier: `inline`'s effect depends on the co-present `static`/`extern`, so a flat `linkageSpecifiers` entry (keyed by token TEXT, context-free, last-wins) would be exactly the clobber `$constexprLinkageComment` warns about — the keyword is IGNORED by kind and the EMISSION decision is made from `SymbolRecord.isInline` at CST→HIR (see `semantics.inline`).

attrSpec.$comment: GNU `__attribute__((...))`. FC4 c1 grew the parenthesized-string form `visibility("hidden")`. TF-C62 (D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE) generalizes the ARGUMENT to `attrArgs` (a balanced list of identifiers / numbers / strings / nested parens) so real-header forms parse — `aligned(16)` (number), `__format__(__printf__,1,2)` (multi-arg), `__nonnull__((1,3))` (nested). It also admits a COMMA-separated run of further clauses (`__nothrow__, __leaf__`) via `attrClauseTail`. THE FIRST CLAUSE'S NAME stays a DIRECT child of attrSpec (so extractOneAttrClause + linkageFrom see it); ARGS live in the `attrArgs` subtree, which `semantics.attributeSemantics.attributeArgRule` names so linkageFrom can FLAG the arg tokens out of its specifier KEY LOOKUP while leaving them visible to the composite `<ident>:<string>` pairing. The trailing clauses nest under `attrClauseTail` so they don't pollute the first-clause name scan (multi-clause HONORING is a pinned follow-up; the first clause is honored). ★ TF-C73 (D-CONFIG-ATTRIBUTE-ARG-RULE-DOCUMENTED-BUT-UNIMPLEMENTED): this paragraph previously asserted that handling as EXISTING behavior while `attributeArgRule` resolved to NOTHING in the whole tree — no loader key, no field, no consumer — which is exactly why the leading-position arg soup survived a full cycle. It is now a real, greppable, loaded key; do not restore prose that describes a mechanism you cannot grep to an implementation.

attrClauseTail.$comment: TF-C62: a NON-FIRST clause in a comma-separated `__attribute__((a, b))` run — name + optional args, nested so it doesn't add a direct-child identifier to attrSpec's first-clause name scan.

attrArgs.$comment: TF-C62: the parenthesized ARGUMENT of one GNU attribute — a balanced `( ... )` holding a comma-separated list of arg items (an identifier, an integer/float literal, a string, or a NESTED `attrArgs` for `__nonnull__((1))`-style double parens). ★ TF-C73: this rule is DECLARED as `semantics.attributeSemantics.attributeArgRule`, and THAT declaration is what makes the special handling real. `linkageFrom` marks every token it reaches THROUGH this node (nested arg groups inherit the mark) and skips the marked ones for the linkage-specifier KEY LOOKUP — so `format(printf,1,2)`'s `printf`/`1`/`2` are never read as specifier names — while the marked tokens STAY in the flattened token list so a LONE string inside still pairs with the preceding attribute name for the composite key (`visibility("hidden")` -> `visibility:hidden`). A wholesale `linkageSpecifierIgnoredRules` skip was MEASURED and REFUTED: it deletes that string, and `visibility("hidden")` then fails H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier on the bare `visibility`. NOTE: the previous version of this sentence described exactly this behavior in the PRESENT TENSE while `attributeArgRule` existed nowhere in the tree (D-CONFIG-ATTRIBUTE-ARG-RULE-DOCUMENTED-BUT-UNIMPLEMENTED).

attrArgItem.$comment: TF-C72: one attribute argument — an `attrArgAtom` plus an OPTIONAL `= atom` tail, for the clang keyword-argument form `__attribute__((__availability__(swift, unavailable, message=_msg)))` (SDK sys/cdefs.h:332, the `__swift_unavailable(_msg)` macro). The assignment is a TAIL, not a new alt, so FIRST(attrArgItem) is UNCHANGED (still the atom's FIRST set) and the comma-separated list stays predictive — no speculation. FIRST(AssignOp)={`=`} is disjoint from the two tokens that can follow an item (Comma, ParenClose), so the `{optional}` is predictively decidable. Operator-expression args (`aligned(2*x)`) remain residue — they fail loud, never silently mis-parse.

attrArgAtom.$comment: TF-C62 (renamed from `attrArgItem` by TF-C72, which lifted the `= value` tail one level up): one attribute argument ATOM. The alt FIRST sets are disjoint (Identifier / IntLiteral / FloatLiteral / string-openers / ParenOpen) so the list stays predictive. The extra wrapper node this introduces under `attrArgs` is transparent to every consumer — `scanCompositePacked`, `linkageFrom`'s specifier-token collection and `decodeAdjacentStringBodies` are all RECURSIVE subtree walks, not fixed-child-index reads (MEASURED: `__attribute__((visibility("hidden")))` still resolves the composite linkage key and `[[deprecated("old")]]` still decodes its message).

stdAttr.$comment: C23 [[...]] attribute specifier (D14: parsed, semantically IGNORED — linkageSpecifierIgnoredRules skips the whole subtree in the linkage scan). Namespaced `[[gnu::attr]]` and a parenthesized string argument are accepted; richer argument forms are residue.

stdAttrItem.$tfc73ArgComment: TF-C73 (D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE): the C23 item's ARGUMENT is now the SHARED `attrArgs` rule instead of the former inline `( {opt stringLiteralExpr} )`. Motivation: `[[gnu::aligned(8)]]` did not parse at all (`P0009 expected 'StringStart'… — got '8'`) because the inline form admitted ONLY a string. ZERO FIRST-set widening: FIRST(attrArgs) = {ParenOpen} — byte-identical to the inline form's lead — so the `{optional}` stays predictively decidable and nothing becomes speculative. Reusing `attrArgs` (rather than growing a second argument grammar) is what makes the C23 form inherit the GNU form's machinery for free: the `semantics.attributeSemantics.attributeArgRule` token flag now covers `[[…]]` arguments too, and `collectAttrClauses` already skips an `attributeArgRule` subtree, so an argument identifier (`[[gnu::format(printf,1,2)]]`) can never mint a PHANTOM clause. The `[[deprecated("m")]]` message still decodes: the string moves from a DIRECT child to `attrArgs > attrArgList > attrArgItem > attrArgAtom > stringLiteralExpr`, and `extractOneAttrClause`'s argument search is DEPTH-AGNOSTIC by construction (it stops at the `stringLiteralExpr` rule, not at a fixed depth — the exact reshape hazard that search was written for).

compositeAttr.$comment: FC16 (D-CSUBSET-PACKED): ONE composite type-attribute — a GNU `__attribute__((…))` (`attrSpec`) or a C23 `[[…]]` (`stdAttr`), REUSING the existing attribute rules. The trailing struct/union attribute list (`compositeAttrList`) is a repeat of this.

compositeAttrList.$comment: FC16 (D-CSUBSET-PACKED): the trailing composite-attribute list after a struct/union body — one or more `compositeAttr` (`struct S {…} __attribute__((packed))` / `[[gnu::packed]]`). Referenced as a TRAILING `{optional}` on structSpec/unionSpec (after `structBody`, so it never shifts the tag's positional index). The semantic tier scans this node (semantics.packed.listRule) for a `packed` spelling. TF-C73: the after-KEYWORD position is no longer a parse error — it is `compositeAttrLead` below, a SEPARATE rule for a load-bearing reason spelled out there.

compositeAttrLead.$comment:
TF-C73 (D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE, CLOSES D-CSUBSET-PACKED-AFTER-KEYWORD-POSITION): the AFTER-KEYWORD composite-attribute slot — `struct __attribute__((aligned(16))) T { … };` (real witness `mach-o/dyld_images.h:124`; 64 of the SDK audit's 204 `aligned` sites, 31.4%). Before it, the shape did not even fail cleanly: `structSpec` swallowed the attribute with its TRAILING `{optional compositeAttrList}` (tag and body both absent at that point) and `T { int x; }` then read as a declarator plus block tail — a FUNCTION DEFINITION, reported `S0018 a function definition's declarator must be a function declarator`, naming the wrong construct entirely.
★ A NAMED RULE OVER A LONE `{repeat}`, so the node is emitted even when the run is EMPTY (the `typedefAttrRun` device). NOT an `{optional}`: `structSpec`'s declaration row addresses the tag BY INDEX, and an `{optional}` would shift it from visible-child 2 to 3 exactly when a decoration is present — SILENTLY, since `extractNameNode` would hand `anonymousNameAllowed` a non-identifier node and a TAGGED struct would bind ANONYMOUSLY with its tag discarded. An always-emitted node makes the index CONSTANT by construction.
★ A DISTINCT RULE NAME, not `compositeAttrList` reused: an always-emitted node carrying that name would be indistinguishable from the real trailing list to any consumer that selects by rule name. This slot reaches the semantic tier through the structSpec/unionSpec rows' `declarationAttrSlotRules` instead.
★ THE ORDER THIS LANDED IN IS THE POINT. This slot was designed, built and MEASURED one cycle earlier and then DELIBERATELY REVERTED, because `scanCompositePacked` then selected the FIRST `compositeAttrList` direct child and `break`ed: a lead slot under a distinct rule name was invisible to it, and `packed` — KNOWN-and-inert in the effects table — was silently DROPPED (MEASURED: `struct __attribute__((packed)) S { int a; char b; };` compiled CLEAN at `sizeof` 8 against clang's 5, where the parse error it replaced was LOUD). Shipping the grammar first would have traded a confusing diagnostic for a wrong layout. The consumer is now surface-count-agnostic — it accumulates every `compositeAttrList` child AND every `declarationAttrSlotRules` slot — so the grammar is safe, and RE-MEASURED it is: that same input now gives `sizeof` 5 / `_Alignof` 1, matching clang exactly.
FIRST = {AttributeKeyword, BracketOpen} (via `compositeAttr` → attrSpec | stdAttr); the slot is NULLABLE and the tokens that can follow are `Identifier` (tag), `BlockOpen` (body) and the spec's FOLLOW — none of which can start an attribute, so the repeat is predictively decidable. Non-speculative, no probe budget.

declarator.$comment: alt of (pointer-led, direct-led): NON-nullable (at least one star or a direct), so `int = 5;` / `int;` stay parse errors; the pointer-led branch's OPTIONAL direct admits the abstract star-only form (`int *` in param position). The branch sequences are INLINE so pointerLayer/directDeclarator land as DIRECT children — the shape the engine's declarators roles describe.

directDeclarator.$comment: Base alt is INLINE + SPECULATIVE: fnSuffix vs parenDeclarator genuinely collide on `(` (C 6.7.6.3p11) — fnSuffix probes FIRST (declared order) under its requireKnownType guard; rollback yields the parenthesized-declarator reading. Identifier rides the token-leaf route (no probe); arrayStarSuffix/arrayDeclSuffix at base are the abstract `int [*]` / `int [3]` param forms. lookahead 64 = the operand-alt precedent (1024-token probe budget): a probe must swallow a whole parenthesized param list / nested declarator. VLA C4c (D-CSUBSET-VLA): the suffix repeat is SPECULATIVE and lists arrayStarSuffix (the fixed 3-token `[ * ]`) BEFORE arrayDeclSuffix so `int a[*]` (a prototype-form unspecified-size VLA parameter) probes arrayStarSuffix first and, on a real bound (`[N]`/`[*p]`), rolls back CLEANLY to arrayDeclSuffix — enabled by the schema-compiler propagating `speculative` onto an inline repeat-alt's loopEntry (grammar_schema_json.cpp repeat arm). fnSuffix still leads (declared order) since it is FIRST-disjoint (`(`).

fnSuffixTail.$comment: VLA C4c (§B 2026-07-14): the POST-BASE (suffix-position) function-suffix `( params )` — grammar-IDENTICAL to `fnSuffix` but WITHOUT the `commitRequiresTypeName` guard. Needed because the suffix repeat is now SPECULATIVE (to disambiguate arrayStarSuffix `[*]` vs arrayDeclSuffix): a guarded `fnSuffix` there would be PROBED even as a FIRST-unique sole survivor on `(` (the sole-survivor direct-descent skips guarded candidates so the binder triage runs), and its `requireKnownType` guard would spuriously ROLL BACK a valid function's `()` (empty params) / cross-file-typedef params — breaking `int f()`, casts, every function declarator. The guard is MEANINGLESS at the suffix position (there is no `parenDeclarator` competitor — that ambiguity is resolved once, at the BASE alt which KEEPS `fnSuffix`), so dropping it is C-correct. Semantically fnSuffixTail IS a function suffix: the `fnSuffixTailRule` config role makes `directDeclaredType` fold it → `FnSig` identically to `fnSuffix`, and the fn-declarator / definition-scope detection recognizes both.

abstractDirectDeclarator.$comment: c26 D-CSUBSET-ABSTRACT-DECLARATOR-TYPE-NAME: the abstract twin of `directDeclarator` for the CAST/sizeof/compound/va_arg type-name tail (C 6.7.7 direct-abstract-declarator). The BASE alt is deliberately ONLY `{fnSuffix, parenDeclarator}` — NOT the full `directDeclarator` base — for two reasons. (1) `Identifier` EXCLUDED: a bare-identifier base would make `(c * c)` (a pervasive multiplication) speculatively commit as a cast `(c *<abstract-decl c>)` — the type child gains >1 leaf so the commit triage's rule-1 'not a lone identifier' fires. (2) `arrayDeclSuffix` EXCLUDED at the BASE (the bare `[N]` form): `(b[0])` (an array-INDEX value expression) would likewise mis-commit as a type-name `b[0]` (base `b` + array suffix). C's direct-abstract-declarator allows a bare `[N]` base, but it collides with the index expression under speculative type-vs-value triage — so the BARE-array type-name (`(int[10])` / `sizeof(int[10])`) is the NAMED LIMITATION D-CSUBSET-ABSTRACT-ARRAY-TYPE-NAME (off the c26 fn-ptr frontier; the `(*)[N]` array-OF-pointer form still works — its base is `parenDeclarator`, the `[N]` rides the suffix repeat). The remaining base forms — `parenDeclarator` (`(*)`/`(*p)` — a nested NAME still parses and is rejected loud at the type-resolve), `fnSuffix` — REUSE the existing declarator sub-rules verbatim, so the SHARED semantic `directDeclaredType` folds it (`(*)(void)`→Ptr<Fn(void)->int>) identically to `directDeclarator`. The suffix repeat KEEPS `arrayDeclSuffix` so `(*)[N]` works. Speculative base (fnSuffix vs parenDeclarator collide on `(`, exactly as directDeclarator).

fnSuffix.$comment: The commit guard fires ONLY when fnSuffix is probed speculatively (the directDeclarator BASE position); the post-base suffix position dispatches non-speculatively on `(` and never consults it. requireKnownType = C 6.7.6.3p11: a lone unknown identifier between the parens rolls back to the parenthesized-declarator reading AND records the ambiguous-type-name candidate for the CU oracle's seeded reparse.

initDeclarator.$comment: TF-C62 (D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE): an OPTIONAL after-declarator `__attribute__((...))` run (`void f(void) __attribute__((noreturn));`, `Tcl_Panic(...) TCL_FORMAT_PRINTF(1,2);`) sits between the declarator and the optional initializer. FIRST(attrSpec) = {AttributeKeyword} is disjoint from AssignOp/Comma/EndStatement, so it stays predictive (no speculation). The C23 `[[...]]` stdAttr rides here too. A run (repeat) admits `f() __attribute__((a)) __attribute__((b))`. These attributes are IGNORED for linkage (they are after the specifier prefix linkageFrom reads); the semantic attribute scan can still reach them via the declarator subtree — noreturn-after-declarator honoring is a pinned follow-up, parse-and-ignore is the first-increment behavior.
initDeclarator.$tfc88Comment: TF-C88 (D-CSUBSET-ASM-LABEL-SYMBOL-RENAME — GNU/Clang ASM LABEL, GCC 6.47.5 'Controlling Names Used in Assembler Code'): `asmLabel` joins the after-declarator run — `int f(void) __asm("_myname");`. The run is the CORRECT home because the label is PER-DECLARATOR in C (`int a __asm("x"), b __asm("y");` names two different symbols), exactly like the attribute it sits beside, and because the `{repeat alt}` admits EVERY interleaving (`f() __asm("x") __attribute__((weak))` and the reverse) with no ordering rule to get wrong. FIRST(asmLabel) = {AsmKeyword}, DISJOINT from attrSpec's {AttributeKeyword}, stdAttr's {BracketOpen}, the following {AssignOp}, and the enclosing list's {Comma}/{EndStatement}/{BlockOpen} — so the repeat stays predictively pruned and nothing becomes speculative. The label is HONORED, not parse-and-ignore: it replaces the symbol's on-binary name VERBATIM (see semantics.declarators.asmLabelRule).

asmLabel.$comment: TF-C88 (D-CSUBSET-ASM-LABEL-SYMBOL-RENAME — GNU/Clang ASM LABEL, GCC 6.47.5): `__asm("<assembler-name>")` written AFTER a declarator renames the symbol. The string is the on-binary symbol name VERBATIM — the platform C mangling (`applyCMangling`) is BYPASSED, NOT applied on top. MEASURED against /usr/bin/clang on arm64-darwin: `int gv __asm("myglobal");` emits `myglobal` (no leading `_`), `extern int f(int) __asm("_myextfn");` references `_myextfn` (the `_` comes from the SOURCE STRING), while an undecorated `caller` still emits `_caller`. This is the macOS SDK's `__DARWIN_ALIAS` family (sys/cdefs.h:791-800 — `__asm("_" __STRING(sym) __DARWIN_SUF_UNIX03)`), which is why the payload is `stringLiteralExpr` and not a single StringLiteral token: the SDK spelling is an ADJACENT-CONCATENATED run of three or four pieces, and a consumer that read only the first body would silently rename to `_`. Decoding routes through the SHARED decodeAdjacentStringBodies chokepoint. Structurally the staticAssertDecl / asmStmt clone (keyword, `(`, payload, `)`) MINUS the trailing `;` — an asm label is a declarator decoration, not a statement, so the declaration's own terminator follows. NOT admitted on a typedef declarator (typedefDeclaratorList takes BARE declarators), on a struct/union member, or on a parameter — a label there declares nothing renameable and stays a LOUD parse error, matching clang.

typeSpecifierForDecl.$comment: KEYWORD/composite-led type specifiers for declaration heads — deliberately NO Identifier arm (the typedef-name head is the ambiguous form, routed through identDeclHead/declOrExprStmt or the committed post-specifier/post-qualifier heads). SPECULATIVE (mirror typedefHead, D-CSUBSET-STRUCT-BODY-VARDECL-POSITION): admits the struct/union/enum BODY forms so a body-defined LOCAL (`struct P { int a; } v;` as a statement) parses; body forms probe FIRST, a ref with no `{` rolls back to the `*TypeRef` form. Single-level. D-CSUBSET-TYPEOF: `typeofSpecifier` (keyword-led, disjoint FIRST) is admitted here so a `typeof(...)`-headed declaration parses.

declHead.$comment: The COMMITTED any-form head: reached only after a leading storage-class specifier run (`register T x;`) — the statement is already known to be a declaration, so the Identifier (typedef-name) arm is unambiguous here.

kwDeclHead.$comment: The keyword-or-qualifier-led head (the non-speculative varDecl statement branch). Qualifier-led admits the Identifier (typedef) base — `const T x;` is committed by the `const` (no expression starts with a qualifier). Keyword-led is the plain `int x;` form. FIRSTs {Const,Volatile} vs type-keywords/struct/union/enum — disjoint.

identDeclHead.$comment: The AMBIGUOUS bare-typedef-name head (`T x;` vs the expression `T(x)`/`a*b`): lone Identifier + trailing qualifiers only. Leading qualifiers/specifiers route to kwDeclHead/varDecl instead (any of them commits a declaration).

typedefDecl.$comment: TF-C72 (D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE): a typedef may carry a GNU/C23 attribute decoration in THREE positions, each a SIBLING of the type-resolved head — NEVER a child of it. `typedefHeadFull` is what `head` points at, and `resolveTypeNodeImpl` picks the head type FIRST-CHILD-THAT-RESOLVES-WINS while its token arm resolves ANY identifier through the scope chain: an attribute identifier placed INSIDE the head is tried as a TYPE, so `typedef int aligned; typedef __attribute__((aligned(16))) long T;` would silently resolve T to **int**. That is a SILENT MISCOMPILE and the reason all three slots are siblings (MEASURED — the anti-hijack pins in test_parser_c_subset_smoke.cpp assert T is long in all three positions, and a negative control proves the assertion is live). The three positions: (1) AFTER the keyword — `typedef __attribute__((aligned(16))) long T;` — carried by the `typedefDeclSpecifiers` prefix below; (2) between head and declarator — `typedef int64_t __attribute__((__aligned__(8))) _OSAtomic_int64_t;` (SDK libkern/OSAtomicDeprecated.h:129,796,799) — the FIRST `typedefAttrRun`; (3) after the declarator — `typedef u_int64_t au_asflgs_t __attribute__ ((aligned(8)));` (SDK bsm/audit.h:199) and the macro-expanded `typedef void print_task_printer_t(const char*, ...) __printflike(1,2);` — the SECOND `typedefAttrRun`. INDEX STABILITY: `typedefDeclSpecifiers` is MANDATORY (it owns TypedefKeyword) so it is ALWAYS the first visible child ⇒ ALWAYS stripped by decl_prefix_strip.hpp; each `typedefAttrRun` is a NAMED rule whose body is a single `{repeat}` ⇒ it emits its node even when the run is EMPTY. So the post-strip role children are ALWAYS [typedefHeadFull, typedefAttrRun, declarator, typedefAttrRun, EndStatement] — the row's `head: 0` / `declarator: 2` never shift, whether or not a decoration is present (the shift-hazard `lowerTypeDecl` documents at cst_to_hir.cpp:8248). Positions (2) and (3) are OUTSIDE `specifierPrefixChild`'s reach, so their attributes are PARSE-AND-IGNORE — the SAME established posture (and same rule set) as `initDeclarator`'s after-declarator run, whose honoring is already a pinned follow-up; position (1) rides the prefix and IS reached by the semantic attribute scan.
typedefDecl.$tfc88Comment:
TF-C88 (D-CSUBSET-TYPEDEF-MULTI-DECLARATOR, C 6.7 — the row opened by TF-C64 on 2026-07-24, whose trigger 'a real header/source uses a multi-declarator typedef' FIRED on the macOS SDK): the single `declarator` became `typedefDeclaratorList` — a COMMA-SEPARATED list of declarators sharing the head base type. `typedef mach_port_t vm_map_t, vm_map_read_t, vm_map_inspect_t;` (macOS SDK mach/vm_types.h:87) was P0001 x3 before this. C 6.7 makes `typedef` a STORAGE-CLASS SPECIFIER, so a typedef declaration is an ordinary declaration and takes the ordinary init-declarator LIST; typedef was the LAST declaration form still pinned to one declarator (topLevelDecl / varDecl / externDecl already take `initDeclaratorList`, structField takes `structMemberDeclaratorList`).
★ WHY A DEDICATED BARE LIST RATHER THAN REUSING `initDeclaratorList` — this was tried on paper and REJECTED as a SILENT DROP. `initDeclarator` carries its OWN after-declarator attribute run, and that run is GREEDY and matched BEFORE the enclosing sequence continues. So `typedef u_int64_t au_asflgs_t __attribute__ ((aligned(8)));` (SDK bsm/audit.h:199) would have its attribute swallowed by the per-slot run instead of the trailing `typedefAttrRun` — and the per-slot run is invisible to BOTH honoring channels here: `declarationAttrSlotRules` matches DIRECT children of the DECLARATION node (the run is one level deeper, inside the initDeclarator), and `declaratorAttrRoots`/`linkageFrom` early-returns because `typedefDecl` declares no `linkageSpecifiers` at all. A shipped, currently-HONORED `aligned(8)` would have started compiling clean at the wrong alignment. The bare list has no per-slot run, so the trailing `typedefAttrRun` keeps EXACTLY the role it has today.
★ It also keeps `typedef int T = 5;` a LOUD parse error (no initializer slot exists), matching clang, instead of admitting it and needing a semantic reject.
★ INDEX STABILITY: `typedefDeclaratorList` is a named rule at the SAME position the single `declarator` held, so the post-strip role children stay [typedefHeadFull(0), typedefAttrRun(1), typedefDeclaratorList(2), typedefAttrRun(3), EndStatement(4)] — the row moved `declarator: 2` -> `declaratorList: 2` IN THE SAME COMMIT; `head: 0` is unmoved. FIRST(typedefDeclaratorList) = FIRST(declarator), so every FIRST-set argument `typedefAttrRun`'s comment makes is unchanged.
★ RESIDUE (loud, never silent), the `structField` posture: a MID-LIST decoration (`typedef int A __attribute__((aligned(8))), B;`) and an asm label on a typedef declarator both stay loud parse errors — a typedef names a TYPE, which has no symbol to rename.

typedefDeclaratorList.$comment: TF-C88: a comma-separated list of BARE declarators — `declarator (',' declarator)*`, with NO initializer slot and NO per-slot attribute run (see typedefDecl's $tfc88Comment for why both omissions are load-bearing). Declared as `semantics.declarators.plainListRule`, the third list SHAPE the shared declarator walk recognizes (after `listRule` = initDeclaratorList and `memberListRule` = structMemberDeclaratorList — the c23 precedent for adding an OPTIONAL second list role rather than overloading the first). `collectDeclarators` yields its `declaratorRule` children in source order, commas skipped, so Pass-1's declarator-mode minting produces ONE Type symbol per alias with its OWN pointer/array/function suffixes folded onto the shared head — `typedef int *P, A[4], F(void);` types P as int*, A as int[4], F as a function type, which a shared-head star could not do. The repeat's exit is INTRA-rule (the `Comma` lead is unambiguous against the trailing typedefAttrRun's {AttributeKeyword,BracketOpen} and the EndStatement), so nothing becomes speculative.

typedefDeclSpecifiers.$comment: TF-C72: `typedefDecl`'s declaration-specifier prefix — the `typedef` keyword plus any attribute decorations that follow it. Declared as the row's `specifierPrefix`, so decl_prefix_strip.hpp drops it before positional-child counting AND `specifierPrefixChild` hands the subtree to the semantic specifier scans (the `declSpecifiers` on topLevelDecl / `structMemberDeclSpecifiers` on structField pattern). It differs from those two in being MANDATORY rather than `{optional}`: the keyword makes it unconditionally present, which is STRICTLY better here — there is no absent case for the strip to reason about, so the role indices are stable by construction rather than by the optional-then-strip round trip. FIRST = {TypedefKeyword}, so FIRST(typedefDecl) is UNCHANGED and `topLevel`'s / `statement`'s disjoint-FIRST non-speculative dispatch is untouched — deliberately NOT admitting a decoration BEFORE the keyword (`__attribute__((...)) typedef …`), which would put AttributeKeyword/BracketOpen in FIRST(typedefDecl) and collide with topLevelDecl's `declSpecifiers`, turning that dispatch speculative. Only `attrSpec`/`stdAttr` are admitted — no storage-class keyword — so `typedef thread_local int T;` still fails loud exactly as before (the 6.7.1p2 note below relies on that).

typedefAttrRun.$comment: TF-C72: a possibly-EMPTY run of attribute specifiers at a fixed position inside `typedefDecl` (used TWICE — before and after the declarator; the `emptyStmt`/`typedefDecl` reuse-one-rule-in-two-positions precedent). A NAMED rule wrapping a lone `{repeat}` rather than a bare inline `{repeat}` precisely SO the node is emitted even when the run matches nothing — that is what keeps the declaration row's `head`/`declarator` indices fixed. FIRST(attrSpec)={AttributeKeyword} is disjoint from FIRST(declarator)={Identifier, ParenOpen, StarOp, BracketOpen}, so the GNU form is predictively decidable and non-speculative. FIRST(stdAttr)={BracketOpen} DOES overlap declarator's abstract-array lead, and the 1-token prune resolves it in stdAttr's favour — harmless because `requireNamedDeclarators` makes a `[`-led declarator invalid in a typedef anyway (C 6.7.8p3: a typedef declares a NAME); MEASURED: `typedef long [3] T;` still fails loud (`expected 'BracketOpen' — got '3'`), never silently mis-parses, and `typedef long A[4];` is untouched because its bracket suffix follows the NAME.

declAttrRun.$comment:
TF-C77 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-LEADING-WITH-STORAGE-CLASS, mode 2): a possibly-EMPTY run of GNU attribute specifiers between an object/function declaration's TYPE HEAD and its init-declarator list — `static int SQLITE_NOINLINE walIndexPage(…)` (the MODE-2 sqlite spelling: 20 of its 119 `SQLITE_NOINLINE` sites, = 16 × `static T SQLITE_NOINLINE f(` + 4 × `T SQLITE_NOINLINE f(`) and `int __attribute__((weak)) gv;`.
★ CENSUS SCOPE, STATED SO THE TWO FIGURES CANNOT BE CONFUSED AGAIN: 119 counts sqlite's `.c` files ONLY and splits 90/9/16/4 = mode 3 (`static SQLITE_NOINLINE T f(`) / leading / `static T SQLITE_NOINLINE f(` / `T SQLITE_NOINLINE f(`; including the 3 `.h` prototype sites gives 122 = 90/10/16/6, i.e. 22 in mode 2. The figure 99 that used to sit here is NOT this slot's — it is MODE 3 (90) plus the 9 leading sites, a position this rule does not cover. Used TWICE, in `topLevelDecl` and in BOTH branches of the block-scope `varDecl` (the `typedefAttrRun` reuse-one-rule-in-two-positions precedent), because ONE attribute must not mean two different things depending on scope. MEASURED at the pre-change HEAD both were P0009 ('expected Identifier, ParenOpen, StarOp, EndStatement, BracketOpen or BlockOpen — got __attribute__').
★ A NAMED RULE OVER A LONE `{repeat}`, NOT a bare inline repeat, for THREE independent load-bearing reasons: (1) the node is emitted even when the run is EMPTY, so the declaration rows' positional indices are CONSTANT rather than shifting by the number of attributes present; (2) the rule NAME is how each row's `declarationAttrSlotRules` selects it, which is what routes it to the semantic attribute scan AND (via `linkagePrefixRoots`) to the HIR linkage fold; (3) the repeat's exit stays INTRA-rule, so `detectAmbiguousAlternatives` never compares the loop body against the parent's continuation.
★ IT IS A SIBLING OF THE HEAD, NEVER A CHILD OF IT. Putting this run inside `topLevelHead`/`declHead` would place the attribute inside the TYPE-RESOLVED head, and `resolveTypeNodeImpl` is first-child-that-resolves-wins with a token arm that resolves ANY identifier through the scope chain — so `typedef int weak; int __attribute__((weak)) gv = 3;` would silently resolve `gv` to the typedef. That is the SILENT MISCOMPILE `D-CSUBSET-TYPEDEF-HEAD-DECORATION-TYPE-HIJACK` exists to prevent, and the anti-hijack pin in test_parser_c_subset_smoke.cpp asserts against it.
★ `stdAttr` IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, and it was VERIFIED rather than assumed. MEASURED with `/usr/bin/clang -std=c23 -fsyntax-only`: `int [[deprecated]] gv;` is an ERROR ('deprecated attribute cannot be applied to types') — after a type-specifier a `[[…]]` appertains to the TYPE, not to the declaration, so admitting it would make DSS accept C that no toolchain does. The exclusion is also what removes the only ambiguity worry: with `attrSpec` alone FIRST(declAttrRun) = {AttributeKeyword}, DISJOINT from FIRST(declarator) = {Identifier, ParenOpen, StarOp, BracketOpen} and from the {BlockOpen, EndStatement} tails — so the run is predictively decidable and non-speculative. The `BracketOpen` overlap `typedefAttrRun` documents is NOT inherited here.

typedefHead.$comment: SPECULATIVE: the struct/union/enum BODY forms collide with the ref forms on their lead keyword — body forms probe FIRST (declared order); `typedef struct P MyP;` rolls back to structTypeRef when no `{` follows. lookahead 256 (4096-token budget): a body probe must swallow the whole member list. D-CSUBSET-TYPEOF: `typeofSpecifier` (keyword-led, disjoint FIRST) admits `typedef typeof(x) T;`.

externDecl.$comment: D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-FN-DEFINITION (§B 2026-07-21): the trailing `externDeclTail` (a `{ block | EndStatement }` alt, the twin of `topLevelDeclTail`) admits `extern` on a FUNCTION DEFINITION — `extern int f(void){…}` (valid C 6.9.1, symmetric with `static int f(){…}`; the Tcl `EXTERN int Sqlite3_Init(…){…}` shape). A `block` tail → a function definition with EXTERNAL linkage (via the row's `kindByChild`, effectiveKind Function, a DEFINING symbol); an `EndStatement` tail → the ordinary non-defining declaration below. See externDeclTail for the disambiguation + fail-loud notes. c23 D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-MULTI-DECLARATOR (SQLite testfixture arc, 2026-07-18): a C 6.7 extern declaration is `extern` + a decl-specifier HEAD + an init-declarator LIST + `;` — the extern-flavored twin of `topLevelDecl`. SUPERSEDES the legacy single-declarator spine (`externSpecifiers typeRef Identifier externTail`), which bound exactly ONE `name` at a fixed child index and P0009'd on `extern int a, b;` (test1.c:9341 `extern int sqlite3_sync_count, sqlite3_fullsync_count;`). The head is `typeRefAllowingStruct` — the SAME star-free base-type head struct FIELDS use (base type + cv-qualifiers, NO pointer stars): pointer stars MUST bind PER-DECLARATOR (inside each slot's `declarator` pointerLayer) so `extern int *a, b;` types a as int* and b as int (a shared-head star would mis-type b). It admits struct/union/enum aggregates (D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-AGGREGATE-TYPE preserved — typeBaseAllowingStruct carries the same specifiers the retired `typeBase` did) + typedef-names + typeof + a `volatile` head (a strict gain over the retired `typeRef`, which had const only). The `initDeclaratorList` is the PROVEN `initDeclarator (, initDeclarator)*` list every object declaration uses; each `declarator` owns its pointer/array/fn suffix, so a function prototype (`extern int f(int);` — a declarator with an fnSuffix), an incomplete-array object (`extern char v[];`), and a mixed list (`extern int a, *p, g[4], h(void);`) ALL parse through ONE list — no bespoke func-vs-object tail. Pass-1 routes through the DECLARATOR-MODE minting (head:0/declaratorList:1) which mints N `nonDefiningDeclaration` symbols; CST→HIR's `lowerExternDeclInto` emits N ExternGlobal/ExternFunction nodes (one per declarator). FIRST(externDecl) stays {ExternKeyword} (unique-production direct descent, non-speculative). TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): child 0 stays the `externSpecifiers` HEAD WRAPPER (`extern` + an optional thread-storage run) so `extern thread_local int e;` parses (C11 6.7.1p3); it is the row's `specifierPrefix` (stripped before the head:0/list:1 count, so the indices are stable whether or not a specifier is present). The REVERSE order `thread_local extern` stays a loud parse error (topLevelDecl's head never matches `extern`). D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-LIBRARY-SYNTAX: a TRAILING `{optional stringLiteralExpr}` after the list carries the DSS per-declaration import-library override (`extern void* GetStdHandle(int) "kernel32.dll";` — examples/c-subset/hello_writefile); FIRST(stringLiteralExpr) = string-openers, DISJOINT from Comma/`=`/`;`, so the list stops before it (non-speculative) and it applies to EVERY declarator in this declaration. CST→HIR's `lowerExternDeclInto` decodes it (extractLibraryOverride) into each emitted extern's import-library map. It sits AFTER initDeclaratorList so it never shifts the head:0/list:1 indices.

externDeclTail.$comment: D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-FN-DEFINITION (SQLite testfixture MAIN harness, §B 2026-07-21): the extern-declaration TAIL — the extern twin of `topLevelDeclTail`. A `block` tail makes the declaration a FUNCTION DEFINITION with EXTERNAL linkage (`extern int f(void){…}` — the Tcl `EXTERN int Sqlite3_Init(Tcl_Interp*){…}` shape, ×14 in tclsqlite-ex.c; `EXTERN` is the tcl.json macro → `extern`); an `EndStatement` tail makes it the ordinary non-defining declaration (`extern int a, b;` / a prototype / an object ref / the `"kernel32.dll"` import-library override — BYTE-IDENTICAL to pre-cycle, only the `;` token now rides this wrapper). FIRST(block)={BlockOpen} vs FIRST(EndStatement)={Semicolon} are DISJOINT, so the alt is predictively decided — NON-speculative, exactly like `topLevelDeclTail`. The `{optional stringLiteralExpr}` library override sits BEFORE this tail (a per-DECLARATION override) so it stays a DIRECT role child (externLibraryOverride's scan is unchanged); it is decl-only, so the pathological `extern int f() "lib" {…}` — a body AND an override — is caught FAIL-LOUD at HIR (H_ExternDeclMalformed, cst_to_hir lowerExternDeclInto), never a silent body-drop. externDecl's semantics row gains `kindByChild` (childPath [2,0] = this tail's block child → whenKind function); when a body is present the SHARED declarator-mode minting upgrades effectiveKind to Function (a DEFINING symbol, isExtern suppressed) and CST→HIR lowers a real Function (body emitted) via the same path topLevelDecl's function-definition arm uses. externDecl is added to `scopes` (the empty scope is harmless for a plain declaration — the topLevelDecl precedent — and dominates the params+body for a definition, via the generic declNodeIsFunctionDefinition scope logic). A function DEFINITION in BLOCK scope (a nested function via `extern` — not valid C) fails LOUD (cst_to_hir block-scope ExternDecl guard), never a silent hoist.

externSpecifiers.$comment: TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): `extern` plus an optional storage-specifier run — the thread-storage twins (`extern thread_local` / `extern _Thread_local`) and, since TF-C77, a GNU attribute run. FIRST(repeat) = {ThreadLocalKeyword, ThreadLocalC23Keyword, AttributeKeyword}, DISJOINT from FIRST(typeRefAllowingStruct) (type keywords / Identifier / typeof / struct/union/enum) → predictively pruned, non-speculative. As externDecl's specifierPrefix this subtree is scanned by linkageFrom: the row maps both thread-local spellings to {threadStorage:true} and ignores ExternKeyword by kind (the extern-ness is the RULE's identity — externDecl mints a non-defining declaration — not a linkage entry).
externSpecifiers.$tfc77Comment:
TF-C77 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-LEADING-WITH-STORAGE-CLASS, mode 1): `attrSpec` joins the run so the glibc/Tcl AFTER-KEYWORD shape `extern __attribute__((__noreturn__)) void die(int);` parses. MEASURED at the pre-change HEAD it was P0009 ('expected Identifier, VoidKeyword, … — got __attribute__').
★ THE ATTRIBUTE RIDES INSIDE THIS HEAD WRAPPER, NEVER BEFORE `ExternKeyword`. FIRST(externDecl) MUST stay {ExternKeyword}: putting a decoration ahead of the keyword would put AttributeKeyword in FIRST(externDecl), colliding with `topLevelDecl`'s `{optional declSpecifiers}` (whose alts include `attrSpec`) at `/shapes/topLevel`, and the loader REFUSES that — MEASURED with a throwaway patched config tree, adding `ExternKeyword` to `singleDeclSpecifier` gives `error[C_AmbiguousAlternatives] at /shapes/topLevel: alt branches share FIRST token 'ExternKeyword'` + `D_SchemaLoadFailed`, at LOAD time, exit 1. The wall is real and loud, not silent — so the leading-position order `__attribute__((...)) extern int g;` is its own anchor, not a variation of this one.
★ ZERO NEW WIRING, AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS SAFE. `externSpecifiers` IS this row's `specifierPrefix` and is MANDATORY (it owns the keyword), so it is ALWAYS `kids.front()` and ALWAYS returned by `specifierPrefixChild` — every prefix consumer already reaches it: `linkageFrom` (via `linkagePrefixRoots`, so `weak` and `visibility("hidden")` are HONORED and an unknown name is loud H000C), `scanAttributeSemantics`, and `specifierPrefixNamesNoreturn` (which is what makes the `TCL_NORETURN`-shaped spelling actually MEAN noreturn rather than merely parse).
★ `stdAttr` is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED. MEASURED with `/usr/bin/clang -std=c23 -fsyntax-only`: `extern [[deprecated]] int dg;` is an ERROR ('an attribute list cannot appear here'). Admitting it would make DSS accept C that no toolchain does. The exclusion also keeps FIRST(repeat) free of BracketOpen, so nothing here can collide with an abstract array declarator.
externSpecifiers.$tfc79Comment: TF-C79 (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-FUNCTION-SPECIFIER, C99 6.7.4p7): `InlineKeyword` joins the run so `extern inline int f(int){…}` and the DECLARATION form `extern inline int f(int);` parse. FIRST(repeat) gains InlineKeyword, still disjoint from FIRST(typeRefAllowingStruct), so the prune stays predictive. The keyword rides INSIDE this head wrapper for the same reason `attrSpec` does — FIRST(externDecl) must stay {ExternKeyword}. MEASURED with clang: `extern inline int p(int){…}` emits `T _p` (a real external definition), which is what this row already produces via its `block`-tail function-definition path — so no emission override is needed here, only the ignore-by-kind entry below.

initValue.$comment: FC5: assignmentExpr (NOT expression) — the comma-gate. Covers ALL three initializer consumers (initDeclarator, structField, braceInitList initElement), so `int a = b, c;` stays 2 declarators (not `a = (b,c)`).

arrayDeclSuffix.$comment: VLA C4c (D-CSUBSET-VLA, C99 §6.7.6.2/6.7.6.3): the ONE array-declarator suffix `[ … ]`, SHARED across EVERY declarator-mode row (param, varDecl, structField, typedefDecl, forDecl, externDecl). It admits the C99 array-PARAMETER decorations — a leading `static` and/or cv-qualifier run before the length BOUND (`int a[static 3]`, `int a[const n]`, `int a[const static 10]`). These are legal ONLY inside a function-parameter declarator; a NON-param use is a constraint violation caught SEMANTICALLY (the paramDecay-gated S_ArrayParamQualifierNonParameter), mirroring the typeSpecifierSeq → S_InvalidTypeSpecifierCombination discipline — the parser is deliberately permissive rather than forking a param-only sub-grammar. The qualifier run is INLINE keyword tokens (they land as DIRECT children, like typeSpecifierSeq's specifier run) and is FIRST-disjoint from the bound (no expression begins with static/const/volatile/restrict), so it is NON-speculative — a plain leading run before the unchanged `{optional expression}` bound. `int a[*p]` (a deref-sized VLA, LEGAL) keeps parsing `*p` as the bound EXPRESSION (unchanged). The bound's CST position is NO LONGER a fixed index (a leading qualifier shifts it) — every bound-locating site skips the decorations via the shared arraySuffixBoundNode helper keyed on DeclaratorConfig.arraySuffixModifierTokens. LANDED (D-CSUBSET-VLA-PARAM-STAR): the bare unspecified-size `*` form `int a[*]` (a prototype VLA-parameter marker) is admitted via the DISTINCT `arrayStarSuffix` = `[BracketOpen,StarOp,BracketClose]` rule (NOT this `arrayDeclSuffix`) + the speculative-repeat-alt schema-compiler engine fix (grammar_schema_json.cpp propagates `speculative` onto an inline repeat-alt's loopEntry, so the suffix repeat probes `arrayStarSuffix` then rolls back CLEANLY to this `arrayDeclSuffix` for a real bound). `int a[*p]` (a deref-sized VLA, LEGAL) still parses `*p` as THIS rule's bound EXPRESSION — the star-modifier is its own fixed-3-token rule, so this flat bound locator is UNTOUCHED. `StarOp` also stays in arraySuffixModifierTokens (the arraySuffixBoundNode scan skips a stray `*`).

arrayStarSuffix.$comment: VLA C4c (D-CSUBSET-VLA, C99 §6.7.6.2p4): the bare unspecified-size `[ * ]` array-declarator suffix — a prototype-form VLA-parameter marker. A FIXED 3-token sequence with its OWN CST node (distinct from arrayDeclSuffix), so the flat bound-locator / lengthChild / captureVlaSize sites that read arrayDeclSuffix's children are UNTOUCHED. It sits BEFORE arrayDeclSuffix in the SPECULATIVE suffix repeat (directDeclarator/abstractDirectDeclarator): `[*]` matches here; a real bound (`[N]`, or the deref-VLA `[*p]` whose `*p` is an expression) fails at the `]` / `*` position and the speculative loopEntry rolls back CLEANLY to arrayDeclSuffix (enabled by the schema-compiler honoring `speculative` on an inline repeat-alt). Semantics: an arrayStarSuffix suffix decays to a pointer EXACTLY like an absent-length `[]` for a parameter; a NON-parameter `[*]` is a constraint violation caught by the SAME paramDecay-gated S_ArrayParamQualifierNonParameter (0xE054).

typeSpecifierSeq.$comment: FC3 c1: C 6.7.2 type-specifier run — one-or-more specifier KEYWORDS in any order (`unsigned long long int` == `long long unsigned int` == `long unsigned long`). The inner alt is INLINE (no named wrapper rule) so the matched keyword TOKENS land as typeSpecifierSeq's DIRECT children — the semantic engine's multiset arm requires all-token children. Which multisets are VALID (and what core each resolves to, per data model) is the semantics.typeSpecifiers table; invalid combos (`unsigned float`, `short long`) parse fine here and reject SEMANTICALLY by absence from the table (S_InvalidTypeSpecifierCombination). The seq SUBSUMES the former single-token Void/Int/Long/Char alts (a one-keyword run). Keyword-led, so castExpr's commitRequiresTypeName triage rule 1 (not-a-lone-identifier) always commits a seq-led cast type. D-CSUBSET-BITINT: the `bitIntSpecifier` rule (`_BitInt(N)`) joins the element alt so `unsigned _BitInt(40)` parses as ONE run [unsigned-token, bitIntSpecifier-node] — keyword-led + FIRST-disjoint, so it only adds `_BitInt` to the element FIRST set (no speculation). A run CONTAINING a bitIntSpecifier is NOT all-tokens → the multiset arm skips it and the semantic engine's bitInt arm (semantics.bitInt) resolves it, scanning the sibling signedness tokens. D-CSUBSET-UINT128-TYPE (TF-C94): the three 128-bit spellings join the element alt as PLAIN TOKENS (Int128Keyword `__int128`, Int128TypeKeyword `__int128_t`, UInt128TypeKeyword `__uint128_t`) — unlike bitIntSpecifier they carry no sub-node, so a run containing them stays ALL-TOKENS and resolves through the ORDINARY semantics.typeSpecifiers multiset arm (`unsigned __int128` is just the {UnsignedKeyword, Int128Keyword} multiset). ★ MEASURED: they must appear in BOTH the leading alt AND its `repeat` twin — the two arrays are independent, and adding them to only one breaks exactly the orderings that lead with the OTHER keyword (`unsigned __int128` parses but `__int128 unsigned` does not, or vice versa). Keyword-led + FIRST-disjoint like every sibling here, so no speculation is introduced.

typeBaseAllowingStruct.$comment: FC7 D-FC7-NESTED-STRUCT-FIELD: the trailing `Identifier` alt admits a typedef-name (user struct/union type) as a struct/union FIELD type. A struct/union body has no expression-statement context, so a bare Identifier in field-type position is UNAMBIGUOUSLY a type-name (no binder-sketch guard needed); a non-type name fails loud at semantic scope-lookup. Tried last, so keyword/tag/enum forms keep priority. D-CSUBSET-STRUCT-BODY-VARDECL-POSITION: also admits the struct/union/enum BODY forms (an inline nested definition `struct Inner { int x; } in;` as a field) — SPECULATIVE (mirror typedefHead), body-before-ref. This makes the body-in-head form RECURSIVE: a structSpecifierBody contains structFields, each of which may itself BE a structSpecifierBody (arbitrary nesting), the recursion falling out of the grammar — single-level speculation at each structField, never nested. c23 D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-MULTI-DECLARATOR: also the extern-declaration head type-base (via `typeRefAllowingStruct`), so an aggregate extern (`extern struct Foo g;`) resolves through the SAME arms — the retired `typeBase` sibling folded into this rule.

typeRefAllowingStruct.$comment: c23 (D-CSUBSET-STRUCT-MULTI-DECLARATOR): the struct/union member-head TYPE-SPECIFIER (base type + cv-qualifiers ONLY — NO pointer stars). The head qualifier slot is `{repeat headQualifier}` (= const|volatile) so a member head admits `volatile int isInterrupted;` (the SQLite case) and `const volatile`; mirrors the head-qualifier slots on topLevelHead/declHead/kwDeclHead. ★ The prior `{repeat StarOp}` slot was REMOVED: with the c23 member-declarator LIST, pointer stars MUST bind PER-DECLARATOR (inside each slot's `declarator` pointerLayer) — a head star applies to ALL declarators, so `int *a, b;` would wrongly type b as a pointer too (the silent layout miscompile c23 fixes). Each slot's `declarator` now owns its stars, exactly like every other declaration position (params/locals/globals). A head-position volatile FOLLOWED by a declarator `*` is a pointer-to-volatile-POINTEE — still rejected loud S_VolatilePointeeNotSupported by the per-declarator typing arm (head volatile + declarator star), so the reject stays complete. The TRAILING slot is `{repeat headQualifier}` (= const|volatile|atomic), SYMMETRIC with the leading slot AND with topLevelHead's trailing `{repeat headQualifier}` — C 6.7.1: decl-specifiers may appear in ANY order, so a base + EAST qualifier run (`int const`, `LONG volatile`, `int const volatile`, west of any declarator star) is a legal type head. It SUPERSEDES the prior `{optional ConstKeyword}` (const-only), which admitted only EAST `const` and P0009'd at a trailing `volatile`/`_Atomic` on either a typedef-name OR a builtin base — `extern LONG volatile sqlite3_os_type;` (D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-MULTI-DECLARATOR; test1.c:9346, `LONG` = windows.json) and `struct S { int volatile x; };` both failed although the leading forms (`volatile LONG` / `volatile int`) parsed. The trailing qualifier is read by the SAME whole-head-subtree const scan (declaratorObjectIsConst) + before-first-star volatile-base scan the leading slot uses (semantic_analyzer.cpp; typeRefAllowingStruct has no head star, so every qualifier child is scanned) — position-agnostic, no new semantic wiring. East const/volatile on a POINTER (`int * const`, `int * volatile`) still rides the per-declarator ptrQualifier.

varDecl.$comment: The COMMITTED local declaration statement — its FIRST set has NO Identifier (the bare-typedef-name form lives in declOrExprStmt). Branch 1: storage-class-specifier-led (`register T x;` — the specifier commits the decl, so the head admits the typedef-name arm); branch 2: qualifier-or-keyword-led (`const T x;` / `int x;`). Inline branches keep the children flat: [localDeclSpecifiers?, head, initDeclaratorList?, ;] — the row's specifierPrefix strip makes head=0/list=1 stable.
varDecl.$c28Comment: c28 D-CSUBSET-LOCAL-TYPE-DEFINITION: the `initDeclaratorList` is OPTIONAL — mirroring the top-level `topLevelDecl` (init-declarator-list?). A bare BLOCK-SCOPED struct/union/enum DEFINITION with no declarator (`struct Sublist { int nList; ht_slot *aList; };` as a STATEMENT inside a function — sqlite3.c:68508 walMergesort) routes through the kwDeclHead branch (Struct/Union/EnumKeyword-led → the unified c25 structSpec/unionSpec/enumSpec defines the type via `definesWhenChild`, minting the tag into the ENCLOSING BLOCK scope), takes NO declarator, and ends at EndStatement. A NON-defining no-declarator local (`int;`) parses + types but FAILS LOUD at HIR lowering (S_DeclarationDeclaresNothing) — the SAME tier + diagnostic as the top-level no-declarator path (CST→HIR's lowerVarLikeInto: no named declarator AND no composite specifier in the head ⇒ declares nothing). identVarDecl's list is deliberately NOT made optional (a bare typedef-name `T;` must stay an expression statement, NOT a no-declarator decl); only the keyword/specifier-led varDecl needs it (the struct/union/enum definition is keyword-led).
varDecl.$tfc77Comment: TF-C77 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-LEADING-WITH-STORAGE-CLASS, mode 2): `declAttrRun` — the mid-position attribute slot — joins BOTH branches, because ONE attribute must not mean two different things depending on SCOPE. MEASURED at the pre-change HEAD, `int __attribute__((aligned(16))) x = 1;` inside a body was P0009 while the identical file-scope spelling was about to become legal; that asymmetry is the defect this branch-pair closes. The run sits AFTER the head in both branches, so the alt's own 1-token discrimination (FIRST(localDeclSpecifiers) vs FIRST(kwDeclHead)) is UNCHANGED and neither branch becomes speculative. Post-strip role children in BOTH branches are [head(0), declAttrRun(1), initDeclaratorList(2), EndStatement(3)] — the row's `declaratorList` moved 1 → 2 in the same commit. Branch 2 has no `specifierPrefix` to strip, and the always-emitted `declAttrRun` is what makes the two branches agree on the indices anyway.

autoInferredVarDecl.$comment: FC17.5 (D-CSUBSET-AUTO-TYPE-INFERENCE, C23 6.7.9): the HEAD-LESS initializer-inferred declaration statement (`auto y = 42;`). NO declHead — the pre-existing varDecl path can never parse this form (declHead's bare-Identifier alt greedily reads `y` as a TYPE name → P0009). The specifier prefix is REQUIRED (localDeclSpecifiers is non-nullable) and semantically GATED: the declaration row's `requiredSpecifierToken: AutoKeyword` makes the Pass-1.5 inference arm fail LOUD when no `auto` is present, so C89 implicit-int shapes (`static x = 5;` / `register y = 2;` / `alignas(4) z = 9;` / `[[maybe_unused]] w = 3;`) that parse into this rule STAY errors — pinned. Probed FIRST in declOrAttrStmt (see its $fc175Comment for the C2 order rationale): it fast-fails (≤3 tokens) on every real-typed declaration (`static int x` — `int` is not a declarator), so ordinary decls pay one cheap probe only when specifier-led.

autoInferredForDecl.$comment: FC17.5 (D-CSUBSET-AUTO-TYPE-INFERENCE): the for-init mirror of autoInferredVarDecl — same shape MINUS the `;` (the for grammar owns it), exactly as forDecl mirrors varDecl. `for (auto i = 0; …)` is VALID C23 (6.8.5p3 admits auto in a for-init). Its declaration row copies forDecl's StaticKeyword gatedMarker so `for (static auto i = 0;;)` stays gated loud (6.8.5p3 violation).

identVarDecl.$comment: The bare-typedef-name declaration statement (`T x, *p;`). The PreferType commit guard (bare-string form — the FC2 triage): sketch-known Type commits, known Value rolls back (`a * b;` stays a multiplication), unknown runs the follower-operator test (`T x;` commits — `x` continues no value reading; `a * b;` rolls back — `*` does) and records the cross-file-oracle candidate on rollback.

declOrExprStmt.$comment: The C statement ambiguity site: FC5 prepends labelStmt (`Identifier Colon …` — a 2-token commit point disjoint from identVarDecl/exprStmt, neither of which has Colon in 2nd position), then identVarDecl BEFORE exprStmt (declared probe order is authoritative — the FC4 c0 fix). lookahead 256 (= 4096-token probe budget, vs the operand alt's 64): the identVarDecl probe must swallow an entire declaration INCLUDING initializer expressions and brace-init lists before its frame closes.

gotoStmt.$comment: D-CSUBSET-COMPUTED-GOTO: `goto label;` (C 6.8.6.1) OR the GNU extension `goto *expr;` (indirect branch to a computed code address). Two alternatives, mirroring sizeofExpr's 2-alt triage. The leading `*` is consumed as GOTO-STATEMENT syntax — so `gotoIndirect`'s operand is the pointer expression `expr` itself (NOT a deref), distinct from the prec-90 prefix `*`. `gotoLabel` keeps the FC5 plain form; the label-vs-indirect choice is unambiguous on the token AFTER `goto` (Identifier+EndStatement is a label; StarOp begins an indirect target). Both lower in cst_to_hir (gotoLabel→GotoStmt, gotoIndirect→IndirectGotoStmt).

labelStmt.$c31Comment: D-CSUBSET-LABEL-BUDGET-CLIFF (p19 Cluster G c31): the shape STAYS `Identifier Colon statement` so a label stays correct in every context, incl. a braceless control-flow body (`if(x) L: s;` — `s` IS the if's body). `commitAfterPrefix` is a PEG cut: after `Identifier Colon` no other declOrExprStmt alt (identVarDecl/exprStmt — neither has Colon in 2nd position) can match, so once the rule's fixed leading token-prefix is consumed in the probe (predictivePrefixLen = 3: `Identifier`, `Colon`, plus the first `statement` token — one harmless extra token, still far under budget) the parser COMMITS and parses the (arbitrarily large) `statement` child NON-speculatively, off the lookahead*16 probe budget. Without it a labeled statement >4096 tokens (sqlite3.c:213922 `json_parse_restart:` before a ~900-case switch) exhausts the budget → rollback → exprStmt → P0001 'got :'.

attributeDeclaration.$comment: FC17 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-STATEMENT, C23 6.8.1): the BARE attribute-declaration statement — `[[fallthrough]];` / `__attribute__((fallthrough));` — one-or-more attribute specifiers followed by `;`. REUSES `compositeAttrList` verbatim (audit-verified side-effect-free: `scanCompositePacked` runs ONLY from a structSpec/unionSpec node, never from a statement). SEMANTICS: the construct is a no-op at runtime — its hirLowering row maps to Skip (the emptyStmt precedent, zero C++); the semantic tier (pass2Post's bareStatementRule arm) runs the attribute scan over it for the UNKNOWN-standard-attribute warning only (facts discarded — no symbol to mark). DSS emits no fallthrough-placement warning to suppress, so `[[fallthrough]]` is semantics-neutral by construction (design note F7).

declOrAttrStmt.$comment: FC17 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-STATEMENT): the varDecl-vs-attributeDeclaration ambiguity site. A statement led by `[[` (stdAttr) or `__attribute__` (attrSpec) is EITHER an attributed declaration (`[[maybe_unused]] int x = 5;` — the attribute rides varDecl's localDeclSpecifiers prefix) OR a bare attribute-declaration statement (`[[fallthrough]];`) — genuinely colliding FIRSTs, so the alt is SPECULATIVE (declared order authoritative, the declOrExprStmt precedent); the bare form rolls back on the immediate `;`. lookahead 256 (= the 4096-token probe budget declOrExprStmt uses): a decl probe must swallow an entire declaration incl. initializers. HOT PATH (design-audit confirmed): every statement lead in EXACTLY ONE branch's FIRST (`int`/`const`/typedef-name/... — varDecl the sole survivor) takes the parser's unique-production DIRECT DESCENT (no probe, no checkpoint), so the wrapper adds zero speculation to ordinary statements. The wrapper MATERIALIZES a CST node (named alt rules do — the declOrExprStmt golden precedent): the statement>declOrAttrStmt>varDecl shape is pinned + the 2 consumers are transparent BY MECHANISM (HIR's unmapped-statement soleMeaningfulChild PassThrough peels it; semantic passes are rule-KEYED full-tree walks).
declOrAttrStmt.$fc175Comment: FC17.5 (D-CSUBSET-AUTO-TYPE-INFERENCE): `autoInferredVarDecl` joins the alt — ★ DECLARED FIRST (the design-audit's C2 MANDATORY order, NOT varDecl-first). Rationale: both decl rules' predictive prefix is 1 token, so a storage-class-led statement (`static …`) keeps 2 survivors and MUST probe; autoInferredVarDecl fast-fails within ~3 tokens on every real-typed declaration (after the specifier run, a type keyword is not a declarator), while a varDecl-FIRST order would probe varDecl under the 4096-token speculation budget and BUDGET-CLIFF existing valid `static const int big[] = {…>4096 tokens…}` declarations (sqlite3.c's largest block-scope static init is 3918 tokens = 96% of the budget — the sqlite gate would NOT catch the cliff). With autoInferred first, varDecl is the declared-LAST structural candidate for a specifier-led statement, so the parser's all-fail REPLAY (parser.cpp ~:1984) re-parses it NON-speculatively with NO budget — a genuine committed parse. Red-on-reorder pin: the >4096-token block-scope static-init test. The only dual-match shape `<specifiers> Ident ;` is invalid C either way — the diagnostic-shape pins (`auto T;` → initializer-required, `auto f(void);` → plain-identifier) hold the boundary. `auto int x;` (C89) still parses via varDecl on rollback — pinned.

localDeclSpecifier.$comment: Local storage-class specifiers + attributes. `static` (D-CSUBSET-LOCAL-STATIC) confers STATIC storage duration (C 6.2.4) — the varDecl row's linkageSpecifiers maps it to {binding:local, staticStorage:true} and CST→HIR routes the declaration to a hidden module-global; register/auto parse and are semantically inert (C: hints/default storage). `static` in a for-init is a C 6.8.5p3 violation, gated loud by the forDecl row. C11/C23 6.7.5 (D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS): `alignasSpec` joins the local-specifier alts too (a block-scope `alignas(16) int x;` is legal C) — FIRST {AlignasKeyword, AlignasLegacyKeyword} disjoint from the others, so the repeat stays predictively pruned; stripped from the child count (specifierPrefix: localDeclSpecifiers on varDecl) and ignored by the linkage scan. FC17 (D-CSUBSET-CONSTEXPR, C23 6.7.1): `constexpr` (ConstexprKeyword) joins the local alts too (a block-scope `constexpr int x = 5;` is legal C23, and forDecl reuses this prefix so `for (constexpr int i = 0; ...)` parses — VALID per C23 6.8.5p3, which admits auto/register/constexpr in a for-init) — FIRST {ConstexprKeyword} disjoint; a block-scope constexpr carries NO linkage (an automatic-storage constant), so the varDecl row IGNORES the keyword by kind (linkageSpecifierIgnoredKinds); the SEMANTIC constexpr validation reads it via semantics.constexpr.keywordToken.
localDeclSpecifier.$threadLocalComment: TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL, C11 6.7.1p3): the `_Thread_local`/`thread_local` twin keywords join the LOCAL alts too — a block-scope `static thread_local int x;` is legal C (thread storage + static storage). FIRST disjoint (distinct exact-match keywords). The varDecl/autoInferredVarDecl rows map both spellings to {threadStorage:true} (Pass 1 marks isThreadLocal); a block-scope thread_local WITHOUT static/extern is the 6.7.1p3 constraint violation Pass 2 rejects (S_ThreadLocalRequiresStaticOrExtern). forDecl/autoInferredForDecl share this prefix, so `for (thread_local int i…)` PARSES — those rows gate the tokens loud (gatedMarkers → S_ThreadLocalRequiresStaticOrExtern; a for-init admits neither static nor extern, so the pairing can never be satisfied there).
localDeclSpecifier.$tfc79Comment: TF-C79 (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-FUNCTION-SPECIFIER, C99 6.7.4): `InlineKeyword` joins the LOCAL alts too, so a block-scope `static inline int f(int);` / `inline int f(int);` declaration parses. Omitting it would be the SCOPE ASYMMETRY TF-C77 explicitly rejected — one specifier must not mean two different things depending on where it is written. FIRST {InlineKeyword} is disjoint from every other branch, so the repeat stays predictively pruned. A block-scope `inline` carries no linkage of its own, so the varDecl/forDecl rows IGNORE it by kind; there is no block-scope function DEFINITION in C, so the emission decision (which only a definition can reach) never fires from here.

param.$comment: FC4 c1: head + OPTIONAL declarator (named `int v`, pointer `const char *s`, abstract `int` / `int *` / `int (*)(int)`). The head admits a lone Identifier — C23 semantics: a lone identifier in param position is ALWAYS a type name (K&R identifier-lists were removed), so `int f(T)` is an unnamed param of type T (S_UnknownType when T isn't one).

statement.$c30Comment: c30 D-CSUBSET-LOCAL-TYPEDEF: `typedefDecl` is admitted as a block item (a BLOCK-SCOPED typedef — `typedef void(*LOGFUNC_t)(void*,int,const char*);` inside a function, sqlite3.c:187603). FIRST = TypedefKeyword, DISJOINT from every other statement alt (varDecl is qualifier/type-keyword/storage-class-led; declOrExprStmt is Identifier-led; the rest are their own keywords), so a unique-production DIRECT DESCENT — NO speculation. The whole typedef-name machinery is ALREADY scope-keyed: Pass-1 binds the alias into `current` (= the enclosing block scope) in the Ordinary namespace; the type resolver (`resolveTypeNodeImpl` SE5 arm) and the parse-time oracle (`BinderSketch`) both walk the scope chain, so a block-scoped typedef-name resolves IN the block, SHADOWS an outer same-name typedef, and does NOT leak out (red-on-disable pins enforce the non-leak). HIR→MIR's `lowerStmtNode` lowers a statement-position TypeDecl as a NO-OP (a typedef emits no code; mirrors the TOP-LEVEL TypeDecl). Mirrors c28 (block-scoped struct/union/enum definition).
