assignmentExpr.$comment: FC5: a C `assignment-expression` — every operator EXCEPT the comma (the two-level expression gate). minPrecedence 15 folds assignment (prec 15) and everything tighter but STOPS before the comma operator (prec 10, looser), so a `,` at a separator site (argList / initValue / enumerator) is left for the surrounding rule's separator, never swallowed as a comma-operator. The top-level `expression` rule (minPrec 0) keeps the comma operator for expr-statements / for-clauses / return / parens / index / conditions.

operand.$lookaheadComment: FC2 Part A: raised 8 -> 64. The speculation budget is lookahead*16 tokens per probe (parser SpeculationProbe); a castExpr probe must consume the ENTIRE cast operand expression before its frame closes, so the old 128-token budget was a correctness cliff for casts of long expressions (and for large compound-literal brace inits). 64 -> 1024-token probe budget.

compoundLiteralExpr.$comment: FC3.5 sweep-c3 (D-CSUBSET-COMPOUND-LITERAL-TYPEDEF): the type position is castTypeRef (typedef-admitting via its bare-Identifier base alt) with the SAME commitRequiresTypeName binder triage castExpr uses. The `{` follower makes most forms unambiguous (triage case 4: BlockOpen is not a continuable value-reading operator -> COMMIT for unknown names); a KNOWN-value identifier `(a){...}` rolls back to the value reading, whose `(a)` parenExpr then hits the orphan `{` -> LOUD parse error (C says the form is invalid anyway).

sizeofExpr.$comment: FC6: `sizeof ( type-name )` | `sizeof unary-expression` (C 6.5.3.4). The type form reuses FC2's castTypeRef + commitRequiresTypeName binder triage — `sizeof(int)` / `sizeof(struct S)` / `sizeof(char*)` commit as types; `sizeof(x)` for a value `x` rolls back to the value form (a parenExpr operand); `sizeof x` (no parens) is the value form directly. The result type is size_t (U64); the operand is UNEVALUATED — only its type reaches the SizeOf node.

alignofType.$comment: C11/C23 6.5.3.4: `_Alignof ( type-name )` / `alignof ( type-name )`. TYPE-NAME FORM ONLY — unlike sizeof there is NO value form (`_Alignof(expr)` is a constraint violation, caught by the type-binder). Reuses FC2's shared castTypeRef + commitRequiresTypeName binder triage (so `_Alignof(int)` / `_Alignof(struct S)` commit the parens as a type; a non-type name fails loud at type-resolve, never silently treated as a value). Single form → NO speculative/lookahead. Result type is size_t (U64); folds to the type's alignment via the type_layout engine, exactly like sizeof reads size.

typeofSpecifier.$comment: C23 6.7.2.5 (D-CSUBSET-TYPEOF): `typeof`/`typeof_unqual` — a TYPE-SPECIFIER whose meaning is the operand's type (typeof preserves top-level qualifiers, typeof_unqual strips them). Two operand forms, disambiguated SPECULATIVELY (parallel to sizeofExpr's type-vs-value alt): the TYPE-NAME form (`typeof(int)`/`typeof(volatile char)`/`typeof(int*)`) probes FIRST, and a VALUE operand (`typeof(x)`/`typeof(a.b)`) rolls back to the value form. FIRST-set-safe: the two brand-new disjoint keyword tokens make a `typeof` lead select this specifier unambiguously in every alt-list it is appended to — the inner alt is where the type-vs-value ambiguity lives, so the speculation budget applies only once a `typeof(` is already committed. The wrapper materializes a `typeofSpecifier` node containing the chosen `typeofType`/`typeofValue` (like sizeofExpr); the semantic tier resolves the inner form's operand and the HIR lowering recovers the stamped result via resolveStampedTypeBelow.

typeofType.$comment: C23 6.7.2.5 (D-CSUBSET-TYPEOF): the TYPE-NAME operand form — `typeof ( type-name )` / `typeof_unqual ( type-name )`. Reuses FC2's shared `castTypeRef` (so `typeof(int*)` / `typeof(volatile char)` / `typeof(MyTypedef)` all resolve) + the `commitRequiresTypeName` binder triage. POLARITY = `requireKnownType` (NOT sizeofType's PreferType default), mirroring `alignasTypeName`: a bare identifier commits the TYPE reading ONLY when it is a KNOWN typedef-name; an ENUM CONSTANT or other non-type identifier (binder-sketch Unknown) rolls back to `typeofValue` and is typed as an expression — the C 6.7.6.3p11-style disambiguation (under PreferType a bare `typeof(ENUM_CONST)` would wrongly commit as a type → a spurious S_UnknownType). A keyword-led type (`typeof(int)`) still commits (triage rule 1). The inline 2-keyword alt at child 0 mirrors alignofType (no wrapper) — visible-child 2 is the castTypeRef (same layout as sizeofType/alignofType).

typeofValue.$comment: C23 6.7.2.5 (D-CSUBSET-TYPEOF): the EXPRESSION operand form — `typeof ( expression )` / `typeof_unqual ( expression )` (reached when the type-name reading rolls back). The operand is the full comma-inclusive `expression` (C23-correct — `typeof(a, b)` takes the comma expression's type). UNEVALUATED (6.7.2.5p2): only the operand's TYPE reaches the semantic tier (via subtreeType), which strips top-level volatile for typeof_unqual; a bit-field operand is a constraint violation (S_TypeofBitfieldOperand). visible-child 2 is the expression (same keyword+paren layout as typeofType).

bitIntSpecifier.$comment: C23 6.2.5/6.7.2 (D-CSUBSET-BITINT): the `_BitInt ( constant-expression )` bit-precise integer TYPE-SPECIFIER — structurally the typeofType twin (keyword + '(' + operand + ')'), a PLAIN sequence (NO speculative parsing: the distinct `_BitInt` keyword + the unambiguous `(` make it FIRST-set-disjoint from every other specifier). It is an ELEMENT of `typeSpecifierSeq` (NOT a standalone type-base alt), so `unsigned`/`signed` compose with it through the SAME C 6.7.2 specifier run, order-independently (`unsigned _BitInt(40)` == `_BitInt(40) unsigned`): the run lands the bitIntSpecifier NODE plus any signedness TOKENS as sibling children, and the semantic tier (semantics.bitInt) reads the width from `assignmentExpr` (child 2 — the comma-free const-expr rule bit-field widths / array dims / alignas / static_assert also use), scans the run for a signedness token (DEFAULT signed), const-folds + validates N (0xE04A-0xE04D + the C1 N>64 gate), and interns `bitInt(N, signed)`. A run mixing `_BitInt` with a NON-signedness specifier (`int _BitInt(4)`) rejects as S_InvalidTypeSpecifierCombination.

alignasSpec.$comment: C11/C23 6.7.5 (D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS): the `_Alignas ( … )` / `alignas ( … )` alignment SPECIFIER — a DECLARATION-SPECIFIER (NOT an expression operand), so it is a SEQUENCE (its tree node is `alignasSpec`, which the specifier-prefix mechanism matches in singleDeclSpecifier/localDeclSpecifier/structMemberDeclSpecifiers). Two spellings: the reserved `_Alignas` (AlignasKeyword) and the C23 `alignas` (AlignasLegacyKeyword). The parenthesized operand is `alignasArg` — EITHER a type-name (`alignas(int)` contributes _Alignof(int)) OR a constant-expression (`alignas(16)`). SEMANTICS live in the semantic tier (semantics.alignas): the value/type is computed + validated (power-of-two, ≤256, ≥ the declared type's natural alignment) + STORED on the SymbolRecord (variables) / fed into the struct's fieldAligns (members). The specifier is STRIPPED before positional-child counting (decl_prefix_strip.hpp) so name/type indices stay stable, and IGNORED by the linkage scan (linkageSpecifierIgnoredRules) — exactly like `__attribute__`.

alignasArg.$comment: C11/C23 6.7.5 (D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS): the operand of an `alignas` specifier — the TYPE form (`alignasTypeName`, e.g. `alignas(int)` / `alignas(struct S)`) OR the VALUE form (a constant-expression, `assignmentExpr` — the SAME comma-free const-expr rule staticAssertDecl's condition + a bit-field width + an array dimension use, so `alignas(16)` / `alignas(2*8)` / `alignas(ENUM_VAL)` all fold). SPECULATIVE, with the type branch carrying the `commitRequiresTypeName` binder triage: the operand position is genuinely type-vs-value AMBIGUOUS (`alignas(int)` type vs `alignas(ENUM_VAL)` value). The guard lives on the `alignasTypeName` BRANCH (not on this alt) — the parser's triage is keyed off the PROBED branch rule, exactly like `operand`'s `castExpr` branch. The semantic tier discriminates the committed reading by the child rule (alignasTypeName ⇒ type form → _Alignof(T); else value form → const-eval).

alignasTypeName.$comment: C11/C23 6.7.5 (D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS): the TYPE-form branch of an `alignas` operand — a lone `castTypeRef` wrapped in a SEQUENCE so it can carry `commitRequiresTypeName` (the guard must sit on the speculative BRANCH the parser probes; a bare `castTypeRef` alt-branch would be probed as `castTypeRef` and `typeNameCommitRule(castTypeRef)` is not set → the guard would never fire). POLARITY = `requireKnownType` (NOT the PreferType default): a bare identifier commits the TYPE reading ONLY when it is a KNOWN typedef-name (sketch/oracle Type); an ENUM CONSTANT or any non-type identifier (sketch Unknown) rolls back to the VALUE reading and const-folds — the C 6.7.6.3p11-style disambiguation. Under PreferType a bare enum-constant `alignas(AL)` would wrongly commit as a type (no follower operator) → a spurious S_AlignasNonConstant. A keyword-led type (`alignas(int)`) still commits (triage rule 1).

labelAddressExpr.$comment: D-CSUBSET-COMPUTED-GOTO: the GNU `&&label` label-address expression. A DEDICATED operand rule (parallel to sizeofExpr) — NOT the prec-90 prefix `&` doubled — because its operand is a LABEL name in the label namespace, NOT a value: routing it through the ordinary identifier-operand path would resolve `label` as an (undefined) variable and fail to parse. The `Identifier` here is a RAW token (like labelStmt's), recovered by the CST→HIR lowering which resolves it to the label's per-function ordinal and stamps the result `void*`. The leading `&&` is the single AndAndOp token (no lexer change).

vaStartExpr.$comment: FC12a-core (D-FC12A-VARIADIC-CALLEE): `va_start(ap, last)`. Takes the `va_list` lvalue (assignmentExpr — the comma-free, non-comma-operator form) and an OPTIONAL second `last` arg that is parsed-and-ignored (the SysV gp/fp offsets derive from the FnSig, not from `last`). A leaf form in the operand alternative list, parallel to sizeofExpr.

vaArgExpr.$comment: FC12a-core (D-FC12A-VARIADIC-CALLEE): `va_arg(ap, T)`. The SECOND argument is a TYPE — it reuses FC2's shared `castTypeRef` rule + `commitRequiresTypeName` binder triage so `va_arg(ap, int)` / `va_arg(ap, MyTypedef)` commit the type position as a type (and `va_arg(ap, x)` for a VALUE x fails loud at the type-resolve, never silently treating a value as a type). The dedicated HIR lowering recovers T from the semantic stamp, exactly like sizeof.

vaEndExpr.$comment: FC12a-core (D-FC12A-VARIADIC-CALLEE): `va_end(ap)`. Takes the `va_list` lvalue; a no-op teardown in the SysV model.

genericExpr.$comment: FC16 (D-CSUBSET-GENERIC-SELECTION): C11/C23 6.5.1.1 `_Generic ( controlling-expression , generic-assoc-list )` — a PRIMARY EXPRESSION whose value+type IS the selected association's expression. A leaf in the operand alternative list (parallel to vaArgExpr). The controlling expression is `assignmentExpr` (comma-free — a `,` here separates associations, so the comma-operator form must not swallow it, exactly like vaArgExpr's ap arg). The assoc-list is a NON-EMPTY comma-separated list of `type-name : assignment-expression` (genericAssoc) or `default : assignment-expression` (genericDefaultAssoc); the list shape (first + `{repeat {, item}}`) mirrors initDeclaratorList. Each genericAssoc's type position is `castTypeRef` + the SAME `commitRequiresTypeName` binder triage va_arg/casts use, so `int:`/`MyTypedef:` commit as a TYPE and a VALUE in type position fails loud at the type-resolve (S_UnknownType). SELECTION is compile-time in the SEMANTIC tier (semantics.generic): the controlling expr's type (after lvalue conversion — top-level volatile stripped) is matched against each association's resolved type for COMPATIBILITY (interned TypeId equality); EXACTLY ONE must match, else the `default` — a no-match-no-default is S_GenericSelectionNoMatch and >1 match is S_GenericSelectionAmbiguous (both unsuppressable constraint violations). Pass 2 stamps the genericExpr node with the WINNER's result type + records the winning association's expression node; the dedicated HIR lowering (hirLowering.genericRule → lowerGeneric) lowers ONLY that sub-expression (its type + value), discarding the rest (the non-selected expressions are UNEVALUATED per 6.5.1.1p3, imposing no constraints beyond being syntactically valid).

genericAssoc.$comment: FC16 (D-CSUBSET-GENERIC-SELECTION): ONE `type-name : assignment-expression` OR `default : assignment-expression` association of a `_Generic`. The `default` form is a distinct alt (genericDefaultAssoc) so the DefaultKeyword lead is unambiguous; otherwise the type position is `castTypeRef` (typedef-admitting, with the shared `commitRequiresTypeName` triage — a value in type position fails loud). The two alts share the `: assignmentExpr` tail shape; the semantic tier discriminates default-vs-typed by the DefaultKeyword child.

staticAssertDecl.$comment: C11/C23 6.7.10 `_Static_assert(constant-expression, string-literal);` and the C23 1-arg `_Static_assert(constant-expression);` — a static-assertion DECLARATION valid at BOTH file scope (topLevel alt) AND block scope (statement alt). Two spellings: the reserved `_Static_assert` and the C23 `static_assert` (both keywords). The condition is `assignmentExpr` (comma-free — a `,` here separates the optional message, so the comma-operator form must not swallow it, exactly like vaStartExpr's ap arg). The message is an OPTIONAL adjacent-string-concat literal (the vaStartExpr optional-second-arg pattern; ABSENT = the C23 1-arg form). SEMANTICS live in the semantic tier (semantics.staticAssertRule): the condition is const-evaluated by the SAME evaluator that folds `sizeof(T)`/enum/arithmetic in an array dimension — ZERO ⇒ S_StaticAssertFailed (message = the string literal), NONZERO ⇒ nothing. The `hirKind: Skip` row lowers a PASSED assertion to nothing in BOTH positions (the emptyStmt/includeDirective Skip precedent), and — because it is a MAPPED rule — makes peelToCore STOP here (never descending into the sole condition child of the 1-arg form).

asmStmt.$comment: FC17.9(i) D-CSUBSET-INLINE-ASM: the GNU inline-asm STATEMENT, cycle-1 = the empty-template optimizer barrier. `__asm__ [volatile] ( <string-literal-template> ) ;` — a structural CLONE of staticAssertDecl (keyword-led, consumes `(` a payload `)` `;`). FIRST = AsmKeyword, DISJOINT from every other statement alt → unique-production DIRECT DESCENT, NON-speculative (the sehTryStmt/TryKeyword precedent). The template is captured as stringLiteralExpr (adjacent-concat + prefixes); the semantic tier (semantics.inlineAsmRule) decodes it and REQUIRES a strictly-empty decoded string, else S_InlineAsmNonEmptyTemplate (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-ASM-TEXT) — a non-empty template carries real per-target instructions we cannot yet emit, so silently lowering it to a no-op barrier would be a miscompile. The optional `volatile` (already VolatileKeyword) is accepted but SEMANTICALLY INERT in cycle-1 (a no-output asm is implicitly volatile — GCC 6.47.2.1 — so the empty form is always a barrier). Operand/clobber lists (`: out : in : clobbers`) are NOT admitted here (the rule ends at `)`) → they fail loud at parse (P_UnexpectedToken on the `:`), the named deferral D-CSUBSET-INLINE-ASM-OPERANDS; `asm goto` (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-ASM-GOTO) and the bare `asm`/`__volatile__` spellings (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-ASM-SPELLING) are likewise deferred (the grammar admits only `__asm__`). The hirLowering row (asmStmt → InlineAsm) lowers it to MirOpcode::CompilerBarrier (the _ReadWriteBarrier op — zero target instructions, full-memory fence).

castTypeBase.$comment:
C11/C23 6.7.7 type-name — the specifier-qualifier-list BASE, and the SOLE chokepoint for it: every type-name position in the language (castExpr, sizeofType, alignofType, typeofType, alignasTypeName, vaArgExpr, genericTypedAssoc, compoundLiteralExpr) reaches its base through `castTypeRef` → here, and `enumTypeSpecifier` reaches it directly. Widening this ONE alt is therefore how a base form becomes available to all nine at once.
★ TF-C101 (D-CSUBSET-TCL9-HEADER-CONSTRUCTS gap 2a): the three composite arms are the UNIFIED specifiers `structSpec`/`unionSpec`/`enumSpec`, NOT the ref-only `structTypeRef`/`unionTypeRef`/`enumTypeRef` they replaced. C 6.7.7p1's specifier-qualifier-list admits a struct-or-union-specifier WITH a member list, so `sizeof(struct { int dummy; })` is a conforming type-name operand (6.5.3.4p2 + 6.7.2.1p1) — MEASURED as what Tcl 9.0's `tclDecls.h:4046` TCLBOOLWARNING writes, and it previously died `P0001 expected 'ParenClose' — got '{'` because a ref-only arm cannot consume the body.
★ WHY THE SWAP AND NOT A SECOND ARM: two arms keyed on StructKeyword is exactly the `C_AmbiguousAlternatives` the loader refuses, and it is right to — one token cannot tell a tag reference from a definition. c25 (D-CSUBSET-UNIFIED-COMPOSITE-SPECIFIER) already solved that shape for the four DECLARATION-head alts by folding body-vs-ref into ONE rule whose `{optional structBody}` makes the split an INTERNAL 1-token (`BlockOpen`) decision; this reuses that rule rather than inventing a parallel path. The binder needs no new wiring: `structSpec` is ALREADY dual-mode registered — the DEFINITION arm in `semantics.declarations` (`definesWhenChild: structBody`) and the tag-REFERENCE arm in `semantics.references` (`isTagReference`, `nameMatch: lastIdentifier`) — and it is ALREADY in `semantics.scopes`, so a body defined here mints its type and opens its member scope wherever the node lands, expression position included. The pre-existing `sizeof(struct X)` tag-reference reading is unchanged: with no body present the reference arm resolves the tag exactly as `structTypeRef` did (pinned by SizeofNamedStructTagStillResolves).
★ RESIDUE, LOUD AND NAMED: `declHeadForParam` still carries the ref-only arms, so an inline composite DEFINITION in a PARAMETER head (`void f(struct { int x; } p)`) still fails loud at parse. That form is legal C but names a type no caller can spell, no consumer needs it, and widening a second alt has its own FIRST-set cost — it stays a parse error, never a silent mis-parse.

castTypeRef.$comment: c27 D-CSUBSET-VOLATILE-POINTEE: the two qualifier slots are `{repeat headQualifier}` (const|volatile, either order) — admitting a volatile-qualified cast type-name `(volatile u32 **)p` (sqlite 67392). The resolver wraps the base in VolatileQual when a volatile precedes the stars, so the cast builds Ptr<Ptr<VolatileQual(u32)>> and a deref of it is volatile; const stays ignored. (Was two `{optional ConstKeyword}` slots pre-c27.) c11 D-CSUBSET-EAST-CONST-CAST: a cast/sizeof type-name admits const PRE-base (`const char *` — west) AND POST-base before the stars (`char const *` — EAST, the SQLite-pervasive form). In a DECLARATION the `*` lives in the declarator so the head `char const` already parsed; a cast bundles base+stars here, so the post-base const slot is what admits east-const. The const resolver IGNORES const for type identity (a cast yields an rvalue), so all forms intern the same pointer type. The two const slots straddle the REQUIRED base token (no ambiguity); a POST-stars qualifier (`char * const` / `u32 * volatile`) RIDES INSIDE the pointer layer (c29 D-CSUBSET-POST-STAR-CAST-QUALIFIER): the leading stars are `{repeat pointerLayer}` (= `StarOp {repeat ptrQualifier}`, c-subset ~500) NOT bare `{repeat StarOp}`, so the post-star const/volatile is present ONLY with a star — NO zero-star adjacency (the c11 ambiguity a separate post-stars optional would have caused). The resolver counts each pointerLayer child as ONE star for ptrDepth and STRIPS its ptrQualifiers: a cast yields an RVALUE with NO top-level cv (C 6.5.4) — `(int * const)p` and `(int *)p` intern the SAME `Ptr<int>`, and a post-star VOLATILE is dropped (no VolatileQual on the cast POINTER) — the c27 PRE-stars-volatile pointee path (`volatile u32 *`→`Ptr<VolatileQual(u32)>`) is SEPARATE and unbroken. c26 D-CSUBSET-ABSTRACT-DECLARATOR-TYPE-NAME: an ABSTRACT direct-declarator (`(*)(void)`/`(*)(int)`/`[N]`/`(*)[N]`) may follow the base+stars — the fn-pointer/array type-name forms (`(int(*)(void))p`, the sqlite osGeteuid cast). It reuses `abstractDirectDeclarator` (the abstract twin of `directDeclarator`, sharing parenDeclarator+fnSuffix+arrayDeclSuffix), so the semantic resolver folds the type via the SHARED `directDeclaredType` (Ptr<Fn(void)->int>) — the SAME machinery a declaration's declarator takes. It is the ABSTRACT twin (Identifier base EXCLUDED) NOT `directDeclarator` because a bare-identifier base would make `(c * c)` (a multiplication) speculatively commit as a bogus cast; and it is NOT the full `declarator` because the leading POINTER STARS are consumed by `{repeat pointerLayer}` above (a star-led declarator's FIRST `pointerLayer` would collide with the repeat — C_AmbiguousAlternatives). OPTIONAL: a star-only cast (`int*`) leaves it empty — none of {fnSuffix,parenDeclarator,arrayDeclSuffix} matches the closing `)`, so `(int*)` stays `castTypeBase`+pointerLayer(StarOp). A NAMED declarator with the name NESTED in parens (`(int (x))expr` / `(int(*p)(void))expr`) parses (via parenDeclarator) but is rejected LOUD at the type-resolve via `S_TypeNameDeclaratorNotAbstract` — never silently parsed as the bare base.

charLiteralExpr.$comment: C11/C23 6.4.4.4: a character constant is opener + coalesced body + closer. The opener is an INLINE token alt (`'`|`L'`|`u'`|`U'`|`u8'`) — token-leaf alt branches consume EXACTLY one token and push it DIRECTLY (no wrapper node; the stringLiteralExpr precedent), so the opener token stays a DIRECT child of this node and charLiteralNodeOf / the semantic char-typing override find it AND recover its SPECIFIC kind (the C23 element-type discriminator). D-TOK-CLOSING-DELIMITER-HAS-NO-TOKEN: the trailing `CharEnd` is the closing `'`, now a real token (charBody's `defaultToken.closeToken` — see $closingDelimiterTokenComment); it is a DISTINCT kind from the `CharLiteral` body precisely so a kind-filtering body reader can never mistake the delimiter for a second body segment. Children go 2 → 3; every consumer locates the body by KIND (hirLowering.charLiteral.bodyToken=CharLiteral), not by index, so nothing shifts.

stringLiteralExpr.$comment: C 5.1.1.2 phase 6 (D-CSUBSET-ADJACENT-STRING-CONCAT): adjacent string literals concatenate — `"a" "b"` is `"ab"`. The first opener+StringLiteral+StringEnd TRIPLE is required; the zero-or-more repeat captures each further triple as FLAT children (sequences inline, no wrapper node), so a lone string yields exactly 3 children. ★ D-TOK-CLOSING-DELIMITER-HAS-NO-TOKEN: `StringEnd` (the closing `"`, now a real token — `string` mode's `defaultToken.closeToken`, see $closingDelimiterTokenComment) MUST appear in BOTH the head sequence AND the repeat body. Omitting it from the REPEAT would not merely under-describe the tree — the repeat would fail to match at the second piece's closer and ADJACENT STRING CONCATENATION (`"a" "b"`) would stop parsing as one literal. And it must stay a kind DISTINCT from `StringLiteral` because `decodeAdjacentStringBodies` selects segments by filtering children on the body kind: give the closer the body kind and this exact rule silently decodes `"abc"` as `abc"` and `"a" "b"` as `a"b"`, with the semantic Array<Char,N+1> typer and the HIR lowering both reading the SAME over-long decode through the SAME chokepoint — agreeing on the wrong length, so no cross-tier guard fires. The opener is an INLINE token alt (C11/C23 6.4.5: `"`|`L"`|`u"`|`U"`|`u8"`) — token-leaf alt branches consume EXACTLY one token and push it DIRECTLY (no wrapper node; the typeSpecifierSeq precedent), so the opener token stays a DIRECT child of this node and stringLiteralNodeOf / decodeAdjacentStringBodies find it AND recover its SPECIFIC kind (the element-core discriminator). Concatenation is at the DECODED code-unit level (each body decoded FIRST, then joined) via the single chokepoint every body consumer routes through. Safe in every use site: primaryExpr, attr args (terminate at `)`), the externDecl library-override tail (terminates at `;`) — none has a string opener in its follow set. Prefix-mixing across adjacent pieces (`u"a" L"b"`) is a LATER cycle — the element core is taken from the FIRST opener today.

argList.$comment: FC5: assignmentExpr (NOT expression) — the comma here is an arg SEPARATOR, never a comma-operator, so `f(a, b)` is 2 args. A comma-operator arg is written parenthesized: `f((a, b))`.

semantics.$volatileMarkerComment: c21 (D-CSUBSET-VOLATILE-QUALIFIER): the language's volatile qualifier token. Read by the type-position resolver's CO-LOCATED pointer arm (castTypeRef cast/sizeof type-names) to reject a pointer-to-volatile-POINTEE (`volatile int *`) position-aware (volatile-before-star = pointee = REJECT; after-the-star = pointer-object = ACCEPT). DECLARATION forms — objects, params, AND struct/union members (c23 removed the head star from typeRefAllowingStruct, so a member's `*` now binds per-declarator like every other declaration position) — reject via the per-declaration-rule volatileMarker (head-volatile + a declarator star); the two arms together make the fail-loud complete.
semantics.$atomicMarkerComment: FC17.9(d) cycle 1b (D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC): the language's `_Atomic`-class qualifier token — the LIVE SemanticConfig-level driver of the type-qualifier wrap, EXACTLY parallel to `volatileMarker` above. The type-position resolver (resolveTypeNodeImpl's CO-LOCATED base arm + declaratorDeclaredType's east/pointer-layer arm) reads THIS token: an `atomicMarker` BEFORE the first `pointerToken` wraps the base pointee (`_Atomic int *` => Ptr<atomicQualified(int)>); an `atomicMarker` INSIDE a pointer layer (east) wraps that pointer object (`int * _Atomic` => atomicQualified(Ptr<int>)). It COMPOSES with `volatileMarker` in the ONE shared {volatile,atomic} bitset skin (cycle 1a `qualified` merges bits, order-independent). NOTE: unlike volatile, `_Atomic` is a NEW qualifier with NO legacy per-DeclarationRule marker — object-atomicity is derived UNIFORMLY from the resolved TYPE (isAtomicQualified) at access lowering, exactly as c27 made volatile do (the per-DeclarationRule `volatileMarker` scan was RETIRED at c27; a parallel per-declaration atomicMarker would be write-only dead config, so it is deliberately NOT added). Source-agnostic: the engine reads THIS token, never a hardcoded keyword.
semantics.$externLibraryByFormatComment: FF6 Slice 2 + audit fold (2026-06-02): per-format runtime library identity for source-declared externs. compileSingleUnit step 2.5 populates HirAttribute<FfiMetadata> per ExternFunction/ExternGlobal by calling synthesizeFfiFromSourceDecls() with the entry whose key matches objectFormatKindName(format.kind()). Per-LANGUAGE field (not per-declaration-rule) — the post-fold #1 placement on DeclarationRule was fragile; the pipeline first-match-loop would silently pick the wrong rule on grammars with multiple extern-shaped decl rules. Library identities: PE → msvcrt.dll (Win32 C runtime for x86_64 hello-world); ELF → libc.so.6 (glibc on Linux); Mach-O → /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib (libSystem dispatcher publishes the libc surface). Per-symbol overrides (`extern "otherlib.dll" int foo();`) anchored D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-LIBRARY-SYNTAX.
semantics.$shippedLibDirsComment: FF11 (2026-06-05) + Model 3 (2026-06-09): the SYSTEM include search path (C's /usr/include analogue) for the angle form `#include <h>`. A directory under src/dss-config/; the header stem maps to a language-NEUTRAL JSON descriptor (`<stem>.json`, e.g. stdio.json) read by src/ffi/shipped_lib_descriptor.cpp — its symbols (name + hir-text signature) are injected into semantic scope before Pass 2, then flow through FF5 synthesizeFfiFromSourceDecls like a program's own extern. Model 3 made each descriptor PLATFORM-NEUTRAL: ONE descriptor per header, carrying a per-object-format `library` map ({"pe":...,"elf":...,"macho":...}); the active compilation target's format selects its runtime image at compile_pipeline resolution (keyed via objectFormatKindName), so a SINGLE neutral directory serves every target. This DISSOLVED the former per-platform-directory selection + D-FFI-SHIPPED-LIB-PLATFORM-SELECT. The full surface (stdio/stdlib/string/ctype/math) + provenance/variadic-exclusion notes live in src/dss-config/shippedLibs/README.md.
semantics.$pointerConversionsComment: D-LANG-POINTER-VOID-CONVERT (step 13.2, 2026-06-02): C-standard §6.3.2.3 — `void*` converts implicitly to/from any object-pointer type without a cast. The two directions are configured INDEPENDENTLY (matching C++'s split, where only the safe direction is implicit). c-subset declares BOTH true (C-family semantics). A future C++ frontend would declare {implicitToVoidPtr: true, implicitFromVoidPtr: false} matching ISO C++ §7.11. Rust/Swift would declare both false. DEFAULT is false (struct-init); strict typing is the safety-respecting default, opposite of the Array→Ptr decay opt-out direction (which is pervasive C-family idiom; void-ptr conversion is a safety relaxation). Pointer arithmetic on void* and void*↔fn-pointer conversions are separate concerns anchored at D-LANG-VOIDPTR-ARITH-REJECT and D-LANG-VOIDPTR-FN-CONVERT respectively.
semantics.$pointerAliasingComment: Two orthogonal C99-derived alias-analysis opt-ins. `strictAliasingOnDistinctTypes` (C99 §6.5): accessing an object through a pointer of an incompatible type is undefined behavior — lets the MIR optimizer's CSE/LICM Load admission prove Ptr<I32> and Ptr<I64> don't alias (Rule 6 in mirMayAlias). `charTypesAliasAll` (C99 §6.5 ¶7): character-type pointers may alias an object of any type — the canonical strict-aliasing carve-out for serializers/hash-visitors/memcpy. C-family languages declare both true. A Rust frontend or strict-typed DSL would declare `charTypesAliasAll: false` (the type-checker enforces aliasing at a higher tier). See D-OPT-LOAD-ALIAS-ANALYSIS for the substrate's design.
semantics.$declaratorsComment: FC4 c1 stage 2a: the C 6.7.6 declarator role vocabulary. The shared declarator walk (name extraction — binder sketch + analyzer) and the Pass 1.5 inversion engine consume ONLY these resolved roles. The pointer/fn/array/group structure lives in the DECLARATOR; heads carry the base type alone.

declarators.$arraySuffixModifierTokensComment: VLA C4c (D-CSUBSET-VLA, C99 §6.7.6.2/6.7.6.3): the token kinds that decorate an array-PARAMETER suffix — a `static`, the three cv-qualifiers, and the unspecified-size `*` — none of which is part of the length BOUND. The shared arraySuffixBoundNode / arraySuffixHasModifier helpers skip these (DIRECT children only) so a bound behind a decoration (`int a[static n]`) is still located, and a bare decoration (`int a[*]`, `int a[restrict]`) reads as an ABSENT bound (decays like `[]`) rather than a runtime VLA. ENGINE-AGNOSTIC: a language without array-parameter decorations simply omits this list (empty ⇒ the plain first-non-bracket-child view, unchanged).
declarators.$plainListRuleComment: TF-C88 (D-CSUBSET-TYPEDEF-MULTI-DECLARATOR): the THIRD declarator-list SHAPE the shared walk recognizes — a comma-separated run of BARE `declaratorRule` nodes with no per-slot wrapper, no initializer slot and no attribute run. It is the c23 `memberListRule` precedent applied once more: an OPTIONAL extra role rather than overloading `listRule`, because the three shapes carry genuinely different per-slot grammar (an initDeclarator owns `= init` + an attribute run; a structMemberDeclarator owns a bit-field width; a plain declarator owns neither) and `collectDeclarators` must descend each correctly. A language that has no such list omits the key and the walk behaves exactly as before.
declarators.$asmLabelRuleComment: TF-C88 (D-CSUBSET-ASM-LABEL-SYMBOL-RENAME): the rule that carries an explicit assembler NAME for the declarator it follows. Declared HERE — beside `afterDeclaratorAttrRules` — because it occupies the same after-declarator position and the same PER-DECLARATOR granularity, and because every init-detection scan (`the first visible Internal child that is not the declarator IS the initializer`) must skip it or it is mis-read as the initializer. It is DELIBERATELY not a member of `afterDeclaratorAttrRules`: that list also feeds the LINKAGE fold (`declaratorAttrRoots` -> `linkageFrom`), which would walk an asm label's tokens as attribute clauses and fire a bogus H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier on `__asm`. Two roles, two keys, one shared skip predicate.

semantics.$parametersComment: C 6.7.6.3p10: a parameter list of exactly `(void)` declares ZERO parameters. The engine applies this at the ONE param-harvest chokepoint when the sole param resolves to lattice Void AND is unnamed; a NAMED void param or void-mixed-with-others is S_InvalidVoidParam. Languages without the flag keep raw param lists.

declarations.$tfc77AttrSlotComment:
TF-C77 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-LEADING-WITH-STORAGE-CLASS, mode 2): the BLOCK-SCOPE mid-position attribute slot — `int __attribute__((aligned(16))) x = 1;` inside a body, MEASURED as P0009 before this cycle. `declaratorList` moved 1 → 2 IN THE SAME COMMIT as the grammar (the always-emitted `declAttrRun` now sits at role index 1); leaving it at 1 makes every local declaration address the attribute run as its declarator list. The slot IS honored: `aligned(N)` written here reaches `scanAttributeSemantics` through this key and applies (MEASURED — `int __attribute__((aligned(32))) x;` on an address-taken local fails loud L_OverAlignedStackLocal, which it can only do if the value reached frame layout).
★★ `unknownStrictAttributeIsError` IS DELIBERATELY **NOT** SET HERE, AND THE REASON IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. It was tried and REVERTED in this cycle. The strict gate fires whenever a GNU clause name is absent from `semantics.attributeSemantics.effects` — but at file scope a second, DISJOINT vocabulary is also legitimate: the LINKAGE one (`linkageSpecifiers` keys + `linkageSpecifierIgnoredNames`), which carries `weak` and `visibility` and which the strict gate cannot see. Turning the flag on here therefore rejected REAL C: `__attribute__((deprecated, __visibility__("hidden"))) int x = 0;` inside a body — a shipped pin (SemanticAnalyzerCSubset.GnuSiblingClauseStringIsNotThisClausesMessage) and clang-clean code — became a loud S0031. A gate that refuses valid C is worse than the silence it replaces.
★ THE RESIDUAL GAP, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: an unrecognized GNU name at BLOCK scope is SILENT — in this new slot AND in the pre-existing LEADING slot alike (MEASURED at the pre-change HEAD: `__attribute__((frobnicate_xyz)) int x = 1;` compiled clean, exit 0, no diagnostic from any tier). This row lists `attrSpec` in `linkageSpecifierIgnoredRules` WHOLESALE, so the linkage tier is blind here by construction. That silence PREDATES this cycle and is not widened by it — the two block-scope positions behave IDENTICALLY, which is the property that actually matters (one attribute must not mean two things depending on where it is written). Closing it needs the strict gate to consult the row's LINKAGE vocabulary as well as the effects table — an engine change with its own design, not a flag flip. File scope is unaffected: `topLevelDecl` does not ignore `attrSpec`, so an unknown name there is a loud H000C in BOTH positions (MEASURED).
declarations.$prototypeSynthesizesExternComment: c86 (D-CSUBSET-BARE-PROTO-EXTERN-SYNTHESIS): a BLOCK-scope bare prototype (`int f(int);` inside a body — re-homed onto the file scope per D-CSUBSET-BLOCK-SCOPE-PROTOTYPE, C 6.2.2p4) that survives with no in-TU definition synthesizes the same no-library extern as a file-scope proto (routed to the module decls, mirroring the static-local accumulator). Same three-way resolution as topLevelDecl's flag.
declarations.$staticStorageComment: D-CSUBSET-LOCAL-STATIC: a block-scope `static` confers static storage duration (C 6.2.4). CST→HIR's linkageFrom folds {binding:local, staticStorage:true} from the SAME prefix scan and routes the declaration to a hidden module-global (internal linkage). register/auto/attribute specifiers carry no linkage and are ignored (ignoredKinds/ignoredRules) so they never trip the unknown-specifier diagnostic.
declarations.$volatileComment: c27 (D-CSUBSET-VOLATILE-POINTEE): `volatile` is a TYPE qualifier (TypeKind::VolatileQual). The resolver wraps the base in VolatileQual when a volatileMarker precedes the stars (`volatile int *` => Ptr<VolatileQual(int)>) and wraps the pointer for an east ptrQualifier (`int * volatile` => VolatileQual(Ptr<int>)); object-volatility is read off the symbol's top-level VolatileQual type at access lowering, pointee-volatility rides the accessed type at the deref/index/member (MirInstFlags::Volatile). ALL pointee/member/param/typedef forms now compile — the prior S_VolatilePointeeNotSupported reject is retired. const stays ignored (no wrapper).
declarations.$threadLocalLinkageComment: TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL, C11 6.7.1p3): both thread-storage spellings map to {threadStorage:true} so the LEGAL block-scope form `static thread_local int x;` resolves cleanly (without these entries the tokens would fail loud H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier on legal C). threadStorage does NOT itself confer static routing — a bare block-scope `thread_local int x;` is rejected by Pass 2 (S_ThreadLocalRequiresStaticOrExtern) before lowering.
declarations.$noreturnIgnoreComment: FC16 (D-CSUBSET-NORETURN): the bare `_Noreturn` keyword carries NO linkage — ignored by kind (like RegisterKeyword/AutoKeyword). The attribute form `__attribute__((noreturn))` on a LOCAL is already covered by attrSpec ∈ linkageSpecifierIgnoredRules (wholesale). The SEMANTIC noreturn scan reads the keyword/attribute; without this ignore the `_Noreturn` token would fail loud H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier.
declarations.$constexprIgnoreComment: FC17 (D-CSUBSET-CONSTEXPR, C23 6.7.1): a BLOCK-scope `constexpr` carries NO linkage (it declares an automatic-storage constant object; only the FILE-scope form has C23 6.2.2p3 internal linkage — see topLevelDecl's linkageSpecifiers) — ignored by kind like RegisterKeyword/AutoKeyword. The SEMANTIC constexpr validation (semantics.constexpr.keywordToken) reads it; without this ignore the `constexpr` token would fail loud H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier at block scope.
declarations.$stringEndIgnoreComment: D-TOK-CLOSING-DELIMITER-HAS-NO-TOKEN: the closing `"` of an attribute's string argument is now a REAL token (`StringEnd` — see $closingDelimiterTokenComment), so it reaches cst_to_hir's flat specifier-prefix token scan. That scan already skips the string OPENER and BODY kinds structurally (cfg.stringStartToken / cfg.stringBodyToken, consumed by the `<identifier>:<decoded-body>` composite pairing), but the closer is neither — untouched it would fall through to the strict `linkageSpecifiers` lookup with the key `"` and fire H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier on the perfectly legal `__attribute__((visibility("hidden")))`. Listing it here also keeps the composite probe's ignored-kind skip-ahead correct, so the closer is not mistaken for the start of a second (unsupported) adjacent-concat piece. StringEnd ONLY: `attrArgItem` admits no character constant (Identifier | IntLiteral | FloatLiteral | stringLiteralExpr | attrArgs), so `CharEnd` cannot occur in a specifier prefix — a char constant there already fails loud today, unchanged — and `HeaderEnd` exists only inside a `#include` directive line.
declarations.$inlineIgnoreComment: TF-C79 (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-FUNCTION-SPECIFIER, C99 6.7.4): a BLOCK-scope `inline` — legal C on a function DECLARATION (`static inline int f(int);` inside a body) — carries no linkage, so it is ignored by kind here exactly as at file scope. MEASURED: this is the ONE block-scope row the keyword actually reaches. `forDecl` and `autoInferredForDecl` declare NO `linkageSpecifiers` at all (a static/thread for-init must ERROR, not route to a hidden global), so `linkageFrom` early-returns on them and an entry there would be INERT config — a probe of `for (inline int fi = 0; …)` produced ZERO H000C before this edit, while the two block-scope varDecl forms produced two. Applying the keyword to a non-FUNCTION is a 6.7.4p1 constraint violation and is caught LOUD by the SEMANTIC gate (S_InlineNonFunction), not by this tier — the linkage scan is the wrong place to enforce a type constraint.
declarations.$alignasIgnoreComment: C11/C23 6.7.5 (D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS): an `alignasSpec` in the local specifier prefix (`alignas(16) int x;`) carries NO linkage — its subtree (`_Alignas ( … )`) is skipped WHOLESALE by the linkage scan (exactly like the C23 `stdAttr` `[[…]]`). The alignment is read by the SEMANTIC alignas scan, not here. Without this the `_Alignas` keyword token would fail loud H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier.

declarations.$forStaticComment: D-CSUBSET-LOCAL-STATIC (MF-2): `static` parses in the shared localDeclSpecifiers prefix, but a static (or any non-auto/register) storage class in a for-statement init-declaration is a C 6.8.5p3 constraint violation — gate it LOUD (never silently lower as an automatic loop variable). NO linkageSpecifiers here: a static for-init must error, not route to a hidden global. The StaticKeyword gatedMarker stays; only the S_VolatileNotSupported gate is removed (volatile is implemented — c21). TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): both thread-storage spellings parse in the shared prefix too — gated loud with S_ThreadLocalRequiresStaticOrExtern (C11 6.7.1p3: thread_local needs static/extern, and a for-init admits neither, so the requirement is unsatisfiable there; WITHOUT the gate `for (thread_local int i…)` would silently lower as a plain automatic — the row has no linkageSpecifiers, so the Pass-1 threadStorage scan finds no entry).

declarations.$comment: FC17.5 (D-CSUBSET-AUTO-TYPE-INFERENCE, C23 6.7.9): the HEAD-LESS initializer-inferred declaration. NO `head` — `inferTypeFromInitializer` waives the loader's declarator-mode head requirement and routes typing through the Pass-1.5 inference arm (single plain named declarator → initializer required → braced-single unwrap → infer → array/function DECAY → loud rejects for void/nullptr_t/unresolvable → stripVolatile → write). `declaratorList: 0` — post-strip children are [initDeclaratorList, EndStatement] (the specifierPrefix strip removes the REQUIRED localDeclSpecifiers prefix before positional counting; varDecl's is 1 because a declHead precedes its list). `requiredSpecifierToken: AutoKeyword` is the ★C1 presence gate — checked FIRST in the arm; without it `static x = 5;` (which PARSES into this rule) would silently become C89 implicit-int. ★M1: NO constMarker/volatileMarker — with no head, the const/volatile fallback scans span the WHOLE declaration INCLUDING THE INITIALIZER (the c58 initializer-const-leak: `auto p = (const char*)s;` would false-mark p const); C23 6.7.9 constrains auto to unqualified plain declarators anyway (`const auto x` is a loud parse error — D-CSUBSET-AUTO-QUALIFIED). NO prototypeSynthesizesExtern (a headless decl can never be a prototype; the plain-identifier gate rejects `auto f(void);` loud). linkage/ignored entries mirror varDecl so `static auto s = 1;` routes to a hidden module-global and `constexpr auto k = 5;` validates through the constexpr hook against the INFERRED type (P1 prefix scan → P1.5 infer → P2 validator ordering, audit-verified).
declarations.$threadLocalLinkageComment: TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): mirror of varDecl's thread-storage entries — C23 6.7.1 admits `auto` beside thread_local, so `static thread_local auto s = 1;` is legal and must resolve; a bare `thread_local auto x = 5;` (no static) is Pass 2's S_ThreadLocalRequiresStaticOrExtern.
declarations.$stringEndIgnoreComment: D-TOK-CLOSING-DELIMITER-HAS-NO-TOKEN: mirrors varDecl's `StringEnd` entry — the closing `"` of an attribute string argument is now a real token and must be ignored by kind, else `static auto s __attribute__((visibility("hidden"))) = 1;` fires H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier on the closer.
declarations.$inlineIgnoreComment: TF-C79 (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-FUNCTION-SPECIFIER): mirrors varDecl's entry, and it is REACHABLE rather than defensive — MEASURED, `inline auto ai = 5;` inside a body parses into THIS row and fired one H000C before this edit. `inline` on an inferred OBJECT is a C99 6.7.4p1 constraint violation, but the LINKAGE tier is the wrong place to say so (it would report a type constraint under a linkage code and pre-empt the real diagnostic); the SEMANTIC gate S_InlineNonFunction owns it, so this row ignores the keyword exactly like varDecl. The `autoInferredForDecl` twin below needs NO entry — like `forDecl` it declares no `linkageSpecifiers`, so its scan early-returns.

declarations.$comment: FC17.5 (D-CSUBSET-AUTO-TYPE-INFERENCE): the for-init mirror — same inference row as autoInferredVarDecl, but like forDecl it carries NO linkageSpecifiers (a static for-init must ERROR, not route to a hidden global) and COPIES forDecl's StaticKeyword gatedMarker so `for (static auto i = 0;;)` fails loud S_StaticStorageInForInit (C 6.8.5p3). TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): copies forDecl's thread-storage gatedMarkers too — `for (thread_local auto i = 0;;)` fails loud S_ThreadLocalRequiresStaticOrExtern (6.7.1p3 is unsatisfiable in a for-init).

declarations.$paramAdjustmentsComment: ★ THIS FLAG DECLARES 'this row is a C PARAMETER, apply the C 6.7.6.3 PARAMETER-TYPE ADJUSTMENTS to it' — BOTH of them. The key is a member of the CLOSED vocabulary owned by the schema loader (`kDeclarationRowKeys` in src/core/types/grammar_schema_json.cpp) and it names the whole rule, not one half of it; the engine helper it drives is named for the same thing (`adjustParamDeclaredType`). ~~ ★ IT IS ALSO THE ROW'S PARAMETER-NESS ITSELF, and the Pass-1 declarator mint reads it as such: a parameter is NEVER a function PROTOTYPE, so `isProto` (semantic_analyzer.cpp) is suppressed on this row. That is not a convenience — the INLINE p8 spelling `int f(int g(int))` writes exactly the syntax a prototype writes (a name carrying a `()` suffix), and without the suppression the parameter re-homes onto the FILE scope (two functions whose parameters merely share a name then collide, S0022 — legal C rejected, MEASURED) and CST→HIR's prototype gate emits NO VarDecl for it, so the parameter SLOT vanishes while the FnSig keeps its entry (`H_UnsupportedLoweringForKind: Function param count 1 mismatches FnSig param count 2`, MEASURED). The TYPEDEF spelling never had either defect — its declarator carries no `()` suffix at all — so only the inline form witnesses it. ~~ p7 (c82, D-CSUBSET-PARAM-ARRAY-ADJUSTMENT): a parameter declared 'array of T' — sized (`int a[64]`), unsized (`int a[]`), or multi-dim (`int a[][5]` -> ptr to int[5]) — ADJUSTS to 'pointer to T'. The flag (a) permits the absent-length `[]` on the param's OUTERMOST suffix (resolving via the incomplete-array path, like allowFlexibleArray) and (b) rewrites the resolved top-level Array to Ptr<element>. An inner-dimension `[]` (`int a[4][]`) still fails loud (S_FlexibleArrayInAggregate via the incomplete-element guard), matching C's ill-formedness. ~~ p8 (D-CSUBSET-PARAM-FN-TYPE-ADJUSTMENT): a parameter declared 'function returning T' — written inline (`void f(int g(int))`) or reached through a FUNCTION typedef (the macOS SDK's `memory_reader_t` / `vm_range_recorder_t` / `print_task_printer_t`, malloc/malloc.h:537,546,550, which are function and NOT function-pointer typedefs and are used bare as parameters) — ADJUSTS to 'pointer to function returning T'. Ptr<FnSig> is already adjusted and is left alone. ~~ BOTH adjustments run at BOTH resolution sites — the definitive Pass-1.5 visit that binds the param symbol (so sizeof(param)==8, and body uses index / CALL through the pointer) and the FnSig param harvest (so call-site checking matches the adjusted argument) — because both sites call the ONE helper. That is what makes a prototype and its definition structurally equal instead of drifting into S0022/S0003. ~~ RED-ON-DISABLE for p8: drop the FnSig arm from `adjustParamDeclaredType` and a function-typed parameter falls through to the FnSig-typed-Variable arm of the bind -> S0018 'function prototype declarations are not supported here'. Suppressing THAT diagnostic instead of adjusting the type would leave the parameter typed FnSig — a function value in a parameter slot, a silent miscompile.

declarations.$tfc77AttrSlotComment:
TF-C77 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-LEADING-WITH-STORAGE-CLASS, mode 2): the FILE-SCOPE mid-position attribute slot — `static int SQLITE_NOINLINE f(…)` (a function DEFINITION; the MODE-2 sqlite spelling, 20 of sqlite's 119 `SQLITE_NOINLINE` sites, census over `.c` files ONLY — see `declAttrRun`'s own comment for the full 90/9/16/4 split and the `.h`-inclusive 122) and `int __attribute__((weak)) gv;`. Both were MEASURED as P0009 before this cycle.
★ THIS KEY AND THE ENGINE'S `linkagePrefixRoots` EXTENSION ARE ONE UNIT. `declarationAttrSlotRules` routes the slot to the SEMANTIC attribute scan (so `aligned(N)` here is applied); `linkagePrefixRoots` pushing every `declarationAttrSlotRules` child as a scan root is what routes it to the HIR LINKAGE fold (so `weak`/`visibility` here bind, and an unknown name fails loud H000C). declarations.$noinlineIgnoreNamesComment:
TF-C78 (D-CSUBSET-NOINLINE) + TF-C81 (D-CSUBSET-ALWAYSINLINE): ★ `noinline` AND `always_inline` APPEAR IN THIS LIST BUT ARE **HONORED**, NOT IGNORED — and the distinction matters, because every other name here really is inert. The list answers ONE narrow question: may the LINKAGE scan skip this identifier without failing H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier? For both names the answer is yes (neither confers binding or visibility), so they belong here; but a SECOND, disjoint consumer — the `attributeSemantics.effects` `noInline` / `alwaysInline` verbs — folds them onto SymbolRecord.isNoInline / isAlwaysInline, through HirNoInlineMap / HirAlwaysInlineMap, onto MirFunc.noInline / MirFunc.alwaysInline, where the optimizer's inlining pass REFUSES to splice the callee (noinline) or WAIVES its size threshold for it (always_inline). Membership here says 'not linkage', never 'not honored'. The loader ENFORCES exactly that reading: its attribute-vocabulary drift cross-check REQUIRES every declaration-attached effect name (any verb but `none`) to appear in this list for a row that runs the strict linkage scan, so removing any of these names from here fails the LOAD rather than silently disarming the effect — the edits are mechanically coupled and cannot drift apart.
★★ TF-C92 ADDS `no_sanitize_thread` AS THE **THIRD** HONORED-BUT-LISTED NAME, AND ITS SINK IS A DIFFERENT KIND FROM THE FIRST TWO — read this before assuming the pattern. `noinline` and `always_inline` are honored by an optimizer PASS that changes its decision. `no_sanitize_thread` is honored by being STORED: the `noSanitizeThread` verb folds it onto SymbolRecord.isNoSanitizeThread, through HirNoSanitizeThreadMap, onto MirFunc.noSanitizeThread, where `mir_text`'s `appendFuncAttrs` prints it as `nosanitizethread` and the parser reads it back. MEASURED: `grep -rni sanitiz src/` returns ZERO hits — DSS ships no sanitizer, so there is no pass for it to switch off and the serializer is its only consumer. It still belongs in the list on the list's own narrow question (it confers no binding and no visibility), and it still belongs in `effects` on the standing rule that a new attribute gets a REAL sink rather than an ignore-list entry ([[D-TEST-IGNORE-LIST-IS-A-LICENSE-TO-DROP]]) — an ignore-list-only entry would have discarded the fact three tiers before MIR, leaving a future instrumentation pass to re-derive from source what the front end had already parsed. So the count of names here that are HONORED rather than inert is now THREE, and the discriminator for the next one is unchanged: does DSS have a sink for it, wired in the same commit.

declarations.$incompleteArrayComment: D-CSUBSET-INCOMPLETE-ARRAY-TYPEDEF (C 6.7.6.2p1: `If the size is not present, the array type is an incomplete type.`): `typedef int T[];` names an incomplete array type. MEASURED as what sqlite reaches on macOS: `$SDK/usr/include/mach/vm_region.h:355` defines `VM_PAGE_INFO_MAX` as an EMPTY object-like macro, so `:357` `typedef int vm_page_info_data_t[VM_PAGE_INFO_MAX];` expands to `typedef int vm_page_info_data_t[];` and was S000B. (The registry hypothesis `an enum constant is not reaching the folder` is REFUTED — no enum is involved.) ★★ THE SIGNAL IS THIS ROW'S EXISTING `kind: type` AND DELIBERATELY *NOT* `allowFlexibleArray`. That reuse was tried first and is WRONG — MEASURED, it regressed VLA typedefs: `allowFlexibleArray` is tested BEFORE the VLA arm in the declarator-mode resolver, so `typedef int R[n];` (a runtime n) stopped building a vlaArray and silently became an INCOMPLETE array (caught by VlaTypedefObjectAcceptsAndRecordsOrigin). The two flags mean different things — `allowFlexibleArray` says `a non-constant bound here is a flexible array member`, which is a STRUCT FIELD rule; the typedef rule is only `an ABSENT bound here names an incomplete TYPE`, and it must not touch the present-but-non-constant case. Only the C-legal position — last, non-sole member of a struct — is admitted, and there it IS a flexible array member and lays out as one. `extern T x;` stays legal, exactly as `extern char v[];` already is. ★ `typedef int T[0];` is NOT admitted by this rule (D-CSUBSET-ZERO-LENGTH-ARRAY-MEMBER is scoped to rows carrying `allowFlexibleArray`, which this row does not) — it stays S000C.
